https://medium.muz.li/ai-wont-fix-bad-ux.summary: The hidden danger of banking’s AI race is not the technology — it’s automating the wrong customer problem with extraordinary efficiency. AI promises to make digital banking smarter, faster and more personal. But intelligence doesn’t automatically make an experience better. Give AI a well-understood customer problem, and it can dramatically improve how that problem is solved. Give it a flawed assumption, a broken journey or the wrong diagnosis, and something very different happens: AI makes the weakness visible. A confusing onboarding flow becomes easier to automate, but not necessarily easier to trust. A poorly timed product offer becomes more personalized, but not more relevant. A support system built around the wrong customer need becomes faster, but not more helpful. This is the uncomfortable side of AI adoption that receives far less attention. AI doesn’t compensate for weak UX thinking. It exposes it. And as banks rush to embed AI across products, journeys and customer service, the real competitive advantage may not be who adopts AI first — but who understands the customer problem best before applying it. https://medium.muz.li/how-to-make-your-b.summary: Practical ways to move beyond generic SaaS aesthetics, strengthen visual recognition, and use AI without losing consistency. LeadHub — Brandbook & Visual Identity System B2B SaaS has a strange problem. Companies want to look professional, and often end up drawing from the same visual playbook. Clean sans-serifs. Soft blue or purple gradients. Dark or very minimal backgrounds. Product interfaces framed inside polished cards. Geometric graphics and abstract tech imagery. None of these choices is bad on its own. But when too many of them appear together, one polished SaaS brand can start to look a lot like the next. https://medium.muz.li/project-palingenes.summary: What happens when you take Conway’s most famous cellular automaton, strip away its determinism, and point it at a Renaissance masterpiece? Palingenesis — from the Greek palin (again) and genesis (birth): rebirth, regeneration, the recurrence of a thing. This is a generative art series that treats a painting not as a fixed image but as a living probability landscape: something that decays, forgets, and tries to remember itself, one frame at a time. Under the metaphor there is a single engine, a heavily modified Conway’s Game of Life. This post is about that engine: how it regenerates, what parameters shape it, and the idea it is built around, which is attention. I’ll use the three works currently public in the series: Lady with an Ermine ( Leonardo da Vinci, c. 1489–1491) Portrait of a Young Woman ( Sandro Botticelli, c. 1480–1485) The Birth of Venus ( Sandro Botticelli, c. 1484–1486) The Game of Life, briefly You already know the rules. A grid of cells, each alive or dead. Every cell reads its eight neighbors and, at the same time as all the others, updates: CELL STATE LIVING NEIGHBORS → RESULT ────────────────────────────────────────────────── alive fewer than 2 → dies (isolation)

https://medium.muz.li/written-feedback-b.summary: Sit in enough design reviews and a pattern shows up that has nothing to do with the quality of the work on screen. The idea that survives is usually the one proposed by whoever speaks first, speaks most, or holds the most senior title in the room. Quiet reviewers, junior designers, and anyone new to the team tend to defer, and their input either never surfaces or gets folded silently into someone else’s talking point. We tracked twelve design reviews across three teams and measured who actually talked. Senior designers took up 42 percent of the airtime on average, product managers another 28 percent. Junior designers, new hires, and interns split the remaining third between them, with interns averaging just 5 percent of a room they were explicitly invited to critique. That imbalance is not a personality problem. It is a structural one, and structural problems respond to structural fixes. The clearest signal came from looking at whose ideas actually got adopted after the meeting, not just whose ideas got the most discussion time. https://uxdesign.cc/bounded-delegation-h.summary: A practical model for deciding what AI can do, what humans must still own, and where product teams should draw the boundary. Image created by the author with OpenAI image generation. An AI tool clusters hundreds of customer comments and names the largest theme “pricing friction”. The label sounds plausible, so the team asks it for pricing experiments, compares the options it returns and begins to discuss a roadmap change. By the time someone approves the recommendation, the important decision may already have been made. The system has helped define the problem, selected a frame and made some alternatives less visible. This is the practical governance question for product teams. Not simply what AI is capable of doing, but what authority it should have while doing it. Capability describes what a system can produce. Authority concerns what the organisation is prepared to let it decide, shape or set in motion. I call the distinction bounded delegation . Give AI broad scope where exploration is cheap and reversible. Delegate analysis more substantially when its evidence, assumptions and uncertainty can be inspected. Tighten the boundary when a team is making a consequential commitment.

Here are seven tasks that put the practice back so we keep human element of user experience and build the bench for 2030. Many teams I know have stopped assigning transcript tagging because now AI does it. Their platform of choice returns sessions tagged, themed, and clipped transcripts before anyone opens them, and does it well enough. Nobody argued, and nobody wrote down what else that task did. Tagging transcripts is how researchers and designers learn that people say “it’s fine” when they mean they gave up, which AI never picks up. Marking redlines is how a new designer learns which spacing decisions the system made and which are open. That work was never worth much as output; it taught the skills needed to repeat in the future so they learned the craft. It was worth a great deal as practice, and the two arrived bundled: cheap judgments under supervision, where being wrong cost nothing. The numbers of this change are already in. I could have started writing, closed everything else, and spent a few hours focused on this, the way I did for most of my working life. https://uxdesign.cc/what-the-bible-got-r.summary: Michelangelo painted God giving life to man. We are the ones reaching now, and the spark has become a string of code. On making minds, worshipping our own creations, and the ancient warnings we ignored to do exactly what it forbade. The first thing the Bible tells you about human beings is that we wanted to be gods, and it nearly killed us. There is a garden, and in it one forbidden tree, the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. A serpent makes the pitch. Eat from it, he tells the woman, and “you will be like God, knowing good and evil.” She eats. The man eats. Their eyes open, and humanity never recovers. God’s reaction isn’t rage so much as alarm. The human, God says, “has become like one of us,” and then, worried the creature will reach for the tree of life next and never die, God exiles them from the garden before they can grab it. That story is more relevant today than ever before. The oldest story in the Bible is about a creature reaching for a power meant to belong to its maker, godlike knowledge, the ability to create and to know, and paying for the reach. Humans don’t create from nothing. We rearrange what already exists. We recombine. Only God, in the story, makes some

https://uxdesign.cc/what-the-bible-got-w.summary: Michelangelo painted a Last Judgment where every soul is finally answered for. We built the first creation that arrives with no maker, no soul, no ending, and no one on the throne. The oldest book didn’t predict AI, but the comforts it promises, a maker who cares, a mind you can trust, a life that means something, an ending that sets things right, are exactly the ones we keep handing to a machine that has none. For three thousand years, being created meant you were wanted, watched over, and headed somewhere. God made us and called it good. We made AI and called it a product. Good is what you call something you meant to make. A product is what you call something you made to sell. The Bible didn’t forecast the data center and the people combing scripture for the barcode of the beast can keep waiting. What the Bible did was make promises, quiet ones, about what it means to be created. There are four. A maker who meant to make you, and meant it in love. A wisdom above you worth trusting even when you can’t follow it. A life that means something precisely because it ends. A reckoning, the accounts settled, someone answering for what happened. Technology has seemingly removed the primary obstacle to decorative detail: the high cost of skilled manual labor. Across various cultures, the rabbit holds a unique place in the human imagination as one of the few animal figures beloved by all. In China's classical Mid-Autumn folklore, the rabbit is a constant companion to the moon—the moon symbolizes the cyclical waxing and waning of existence, while the rabbit metaphorically represents the vitality, growth, and flourishing of all beings.

https://www.archdaily.com/1040166/qing-s.summary: Qingshuiyan Ancestral Hall Supporting Facility Renovation Set within the core scenic area of the thousand-year-old Qingshuiyan Ancestral Hall in Anxi, Quanzhou , this project renovates a decommissioned old bus station left unused after its functional relocation. The site is anchored by a moss-draped ancient banyan tree at the center of a forest-framed open square, with a dilapidated two-story station building, native rock formations, and ancient mossy paths defining its unique natural and historic context. First built in the Northern Song Dynasty, Qingshuiyan Ancestral Hall sits at the northern foot of perennially mist-shrouded Penglai Mountain. As a vital folk belief center for Fujian, Taiwan and Southeast Asian communities with over 100 million believers, the hall shaped the project's core ethos of harmony with nature and local heritage. The in-situ renovation integrates tea houses, vegetarian restaurants, and rest areas as a complementary facility for the ancestral hall.
https://www.archdaily.com/1040166/qing-s.title: Qing Shui Meditation Retreat Center / RESP Studio

https://www.archdaily.com/1041129/beauty.summary: Xu Tiantian is the founding principal of DnA_Design and Architecture , an interdisciplinary practice that addresses both the physical and social dimensions of the contemporary living environment, across scales. Born in 1975 in Fujian , China , she received a Master of Architecture in Urban Design from the Harvard Graduate School of Design and a bachelor's degree in architecture from Tsinghua University in Beijing. Her recent work focuses on rural revitalization through a strategy she describes as "architectural acupuncture," understood as small-scale, site-specific interventions designed to activate local culture, agriculture, and tourism. These interventions, primarily concentrated in China's rural regions , have been recognized by UN-Habitat as a global model for urban–rural integration. In this interview with Louisiana Channel , she reflects on the role of the architect, questions architecture itself and the concept of beauty, explains her working methodology, and emphasizes the spatial dimension of nature.

https://www.archdaily.com/1183933/bigger.summary: Seamless surfaces and minimal joints have become a defining signature of contemporary architecture, prized for the clean lines, and uniformity they bring to a building's envelope. Yet in façade engineering, this pursuit is rarely just about appearance. Regardless of the material used, increasing panel dimensions can influence durability, material recyclability, performance against external factors, and other considerations such as impact resistance and long-term maintenance. By combining ease of installation and transportation efficiency with design flexibility, monomaterial façade systems use large-format panels while addressing practical challenges related to flatness, thermal movement, and structural support. Yet, what other material-related considerations behind large-format panels can make a difference in building envelope construction today?
https://www.archdaily.com/1183933/bigger.title: Bigger Isn't Just an Aesthetic Choice: What Façade Systems Conceal Behind Their Materials

https://www.archdaily.com/1184648/above-.summary: There is no harder place to build than a high mountain, and none where a building feels more provisional. From the Andes to the Himalaya to the Alps , high-altitude construction strips architecture back to its most elementary transactions. The rock reads as permanence itself, yet a structure set near the limit of habitation exists in negotiation with almost everything around it: with wind that arrives without obstruction, with a ground too steep and too frozen to excavate, and with everything it needs arriving from far below. What can be carried up, what can be assembled by few hands, and what can sustain itself are some of the terms of the problem.
https://www.archdaily.com/1184648/above-.title: Above the Snowline: 11 Shelters Built at the Limits of Construction

https://www.archdaily.com/1185014/the-er.summary: The office chair has evolved alongside changing workplaces over time. In each office era, the chair has reflected the way people work. Early office seating was built for clerical work: fixed wooden chairs arranged in rows across large administrative offices, where paperwork followed standardized routines. By the 1980s, computers began changing how people occupied a desk, and office furniture followed. Designers approached seating through ergonomics and biomechanics, refining adjustable height, lumbar support, synchronized recline, and the relationship between the body and the workstation. Later designers combined ergonomic research with new materials such as breathable suspension mesh instead of conventional foam upholstery.
https://www.archdaily.com/1185014/the-er.title: The Ergonomic Office Chair in the Age of AI

By 2001, after more than fifty years of continuous operation, Fresh Kills covered 2,200 acres, roughly three times the area of Central Park , and was, unspectacularly, visible from space. When it started, Moses didn't expect to design a dump but, without calling it that, a new landform with four artificial hills rising up to sixty meters above sea level built entirely from the accumulated residue of eight million daily lives.

https://www.archdaily.com/1185525/spiral.summary: In most architectural projects, vertical circulation is expressed as a purely functional element , tucked away behind fire-rated doors or an elevator core. However, sometimes architects also use spirals when trying to resolve site elevation changes. Given the right scale, these elements allow for a more artistic formal expression that serves both utilitarian and aesthetic purposes without relying on mechanical lifts or stairwells. Structural systems like cantilevered steel trusses and reinforced concrete decks allow these spiral elements to extend outward as sheltered entry canopies or wind around open central atriums. Functionally, these circulation paths may be expressed in several ways: as stairs like the Itamaraty Palace in Brasilia, or as ramps, which can offer the possibility to reduce mobility barriers for visitors. In both cases, the spiral can provide smooth transitions across varied floor levels while maintaining an unobstructed line-of-sight throughout the program.

https://www.archdaily.com/1185860/beyond.summary: "Let us take a hard look at the facts." The document taught families how to build shelters capable of protecting them from radioactive fallout after a possible nuclear attack and, through technical drawings and sketches, outlined solutions using concrete blocks, walls filled with earth or sand, underground structures, and ventilation systems. It was a survival manual that, in many ways, also functioned as a construction manual.

https://www.archdaily.com/1185867/citize.summary: A campaign led by Red Lima Milenaria is seeking UNESCO recognition for pre-colonial sites in the Peruvian capital. Today, more than 600 archaeological sites remain in Lima , a metropolis of 11 million people. The citizens' campaign seeks to improve conservation conditions and public awareness of the sites that resisted European colonization by promoting the nomination of a selection of structures for inscription on UNESCO's World Heritage List . The public campaign was recently launched to gather citizen support and establish partnerships with organizations working in heritage and related fields, in order to prepare the framework for a formal nomination to be submitted by the Peruvian state. The initiative coincides with reconstruction movements in the continent responding to socioeconomic inequality and structural historical injustices, raising questions about the very definition of heritage.
https://www.archdaily.com/1185867/citize.title: Citizen-Led Campaign Seeks UNESCO Status for Select Pre-Colonial Sites in Lima, Peru

https://www.archdaily.com/1185868/danish.summary: For the second year running, Copenhagen was named the world's most livable city in the 2026 Economist Intelligence Unit's Global Liveability Index . According to the Danish Architecture Center , part of this progress in urban quality of life is due to the work of Danish architect and urban planner Jan Gehl , who celebrates his 90th birthday this year. Jan Gehl has dedicated his professional career to the field of city life and people-centered urban development, founding Gehl Architects (now Gehl Studio) in 2000 and publishing extensively on urban design methodologies to create lively, healthy, and human-centric urban environments. In honor of his birthday, the Danish Architecture Center is presenting an exhibition and a series of activities centered on the role he has played in urban development worldwide.
https://www.archdaily.com/1185868/danish.title: Danish Architecture Center Celebrates Urbanist Jan Gehl's 90th Birthday with a Calendar of Activities and an Exhibition

https://www.archdaily.com/1185903/zanine.summary: Zanine Caldas – Creating Worlds runs through November 7, 2026, at the Tomie Ohtake House-Studio, the artist's former residence in Campo Belo, São Paulo. Curated by Sabrina Fontenele with assistance from Lahayda Mamani Poma, the exhibition brings together furniture, models, drawings, architectural projects, photographs, films, and documents from different moments in the career of José Zanine Caldas (1919–2001). https://www.archdaily.com/1185940/a-new-.summary: What makes a building worth preserving? Age is the most common answer, but not always the best one. A building from the 1950s or 70s may carry as much historical significance as a medieval cathedral; it simply demands a different framework, one that weighs political context, cultural meaning, and architectural innovation over the mere passage of time. This is especially true for modernist architecture across the so-called Global South , where the movement took on unique forms of expression.

https://www.archdaily.com/1185958/necess.summary: The landscape and scattered settlements of Ireland carry a reputation for wildness. Rugged cliffs meet the Atlantic, green fields roll across the interior, and rain and wind change the scene by the hour. A closer look reveals a worked terrain as historic stone walls divide agricultural fields, r oads and paths connect towns to the coast, and castle ruins alongside cottages record centuries of occupation. Change is the expected condition of the island, shaped as much by human hands as by geology and weather, and the practice of treating the existing context as material to adapt and modify runs deep.

https://www.archdaily.com/1186027/the-lu.summary: A jury of arts and architecture professionals recently announced the selected curatorial proposal for the Luxembourg Pavilion at the Biennale Architettura 2027 . The proposal is titled "Excess! On the Overconsumption of Living Space" and addresses the inequitable distribution of living space as a reflection of "broader habits of excess that contribute to the current housing and ecological crises." The issue will be illustrated through a dialogue between the realities of Luxembourg and Vietnam to reflect on spatial consumption. The Luxembourg Pavilion is located on the first floor of the Sale d'Armi in the Arsenale , which will open to the public for the Biennale on May 8, 2027.

https://www.archdaily.com/1186439/henn-l.summary: Architecture firm HENN has launched CarbonBudget , a digital tool that calculates project-specific CO2 budgets for buildings. As the construction industry is responsible for around one-third of global CO2 emissions, architectural design decisions can effectively contribute to containing global warming. The tool is designed to calculate whether the emissions of a building project located in Europe are compatible with the Paris Agreement target, based on specific inputs such as location and building area. https://www.behance.net/gallery/25602724.summary: Vexto is a desktop app that gives our dispatch team real-time visibility into every vehicle in the fleet. It brings live GPS tracking, accident detection, and webcam verification into one system, so we can confirm incidents faster, respond with full context, and keep the whole operation under control. The project moved from fleet data audit to system architecture, incident logic, and map-based UX flows. Time was spent aligning live GPS, accident detection, and webcam feeds into one platform. The deepest work was structuring real-time logic that stays reliable at scale. We prioritized map-first navigation over list-based menus, since dispatchers think in location, not records. Analysis showed incident context mattered more than raw data, so we surfaced vehicle status, connectivity, and live webcam access in one card ? cutting verification time and improving response control.

https://www.core77.com/posts/145407/LDF-.summary: Much has been said and written about design festivals having to bow to economic restraints and corporate rule. This year, independent collectives across London got together to shake up the establishment by just doing it themselves, together. I visited two exhibitions that stood out not only for giving space to emerging talent, but for offering a welcome shift from polished showrooms and stark galleries: relaxed, immersive spaces that invited you to hang out, interact and explore. Design Everything began after London designer Lewis Duckworth was quoted £900 per square metre to exhibit at LDF and decided to create his own show. https://www.core77.com/posts/145443/Cost.summary: This year Volvo brought the EX30 , an electric SUV, to the U.S. market. (In Europe the car has been available since 2023, but tariffs and red tape delayed the U.S. launch.) Starting around $38,000, it's meant to be an affordable EV and gateway vehicle to the brand. The car looks smart enough on the outside, but the interior is a damning indictment of cost-cutting. Multiple speakers have been eliminated in favor of a single soundbar, to reduce wiring, but that's the least of the troubles. Take a look at the dashboard: That's right, there's no instrument cluster behind the steering wheel. That little black thing you see houses a driver-monitoring camera. To see your current speed, you need to flick your gaze sideways to the central screen. There is no option for a heads-up display. There's also no buttons, knobs or switches on the dash. Instead you must use the touchscreen for climate control, to adjust your headlight settings, select your wiper sensitivity and even open the glovebox. I know that Tesla owners are already accustomed to this trade-off. However, I find it surprising from Volvo's designers because the brand built their name on safety. https://www.core77.com/posts/145462/An-A.summary: In the 1960s, college students stumbled across an abandoned ruin in the wilds of Warsaw, Virginia, outside of Richmond. The crumbling stone structure had been abandoned following a hurricane in the 1930s, and weather had taken its toll. It presumably made for a great party spot for the co-eds. As it turns out, the house had historic significance and was older than America. Callled Menokin , it was built in 1769 by Revolutionary leader Francis Lightfoot Lee, a signer of the Declaration of Independence. When the abandoned house was a little over 200 years old, in the 1970s, it suffered a major structural collapse. By the 1990s, a group of historic preservation advocates formed the nonprofit Menokin Foundation, to raise money to save the building. It took until the 2000s to put together enough cash to start, and form a plan. Preservation architects Charles Phillips and John Lee proposed the missing parts of the house be replaced not with masonry, but with glass, in a sort of architectural-scale kintsugi. The concept was radical, but agreed to by the Foundation. In 2013, Boston-based architecture firm Machado Silvetti won the bid to design its actual construction. Work didn't actually
https://www.core77.com/posts/145462/An-A.title: An Architectural-Scale Kintsugi Project

https://www.core77.com/posts/145476/Raak.summary: ENT doctors use nasal speculums to look inside a patient's nose. Typically the tool is held in one hand and a flashlight in the other. Belgian industrial design firm Raak Design streamlined this approach with their new speculum design for client VisionTech. They've managed to snake a tube up the inside of the handle with an LED at the end, providing light right where the doctor needs it. The electronic component is hidden in the handle, and was designed to be removable for autoclaving (sterilization) of the tool. Mechanically speaking, "The spring mechanism is fully enclosed within the sculpted handle," the firm writes, "creating a precise grip and a calmer, more approachable appearance for both clinicians and patients. "The result is a refined medical tool that improves visibility, simplifies the examination workflow, and is engineered for dependable everyday clinical use."

https://www.core77.com/posts/145479/Mafe.summary: Traditional timber framing is still very much a thing in Europe. Timber framers often need to drill accurate holes for the pegs that will fasten two timbers, and these holes occasionally need to be drilled at angles. The designers at Mafell, the German power tool manufacturer, found that existing drill guides weren't up to snuff for timber framers and their massive workpieces. Incumbent designs typically plunge on two skinny rods that can flex, and the angle adjustments move the point of entry for the drill, complicating marking. They designed their BST 460 S drilling station to eliminate these pain points. The 460 S ditches the dual-rod arrangement, offering a single beefy aluminum extrusion with more rigidity and better visibility of the mark. The hinge mechanism was designed so that the drill tip always serves as the pivot axis. The designers also added six rollers, in two pairs of three, that encircle the bit in an iris-style enclosure. This prevents the bit from wandering. Here's a demo:

https://www.core77.com/posts/145488/AI-H.summary: For most of my nearly three decades teaching design at Parsons School of Design , there was a relatively straightforward answer to the question of what made a young designer valuable: technical proficiency. Students needed to know how to draw, construct, render, prototype, photograph, present, and eventually master whatever digital tools were transforming the profession. The tools changed constantly. The underlying expectation did not. Then AI arrived. Today, a designer can generate polished images, presentations, variations, and even entire visual directions in minutes. The ability to produce is becoming abundant—and when production becomes abundant, something else becomes scarce. Judgment. This shift has consequences far beyond design schools. It should change how organizations hire designers, evaluate creative work, cultivate junior talent, and structure the creative process itself. The organizations that adapt will not be those that simply give designers better AI tools. They will be the ones that understand that the value of a designer is increasingly determined before anything gets made. The competitive advantage has moved upstream Five years ago, I might have told a design s

https://www.core77.com/posts/145494/How-.summary: In the 1970s, Ernest Emerson was a machinist at Hughes Aircraft, an aerospace and defense company outside of L.A. Emerson was also an accomplished martial artist, having trained since childhood; the reason he moved from his native Wisconsin to California was not to work at Hughes, but to train at the Filipino Kali Academy run by the legendary Dan Inosanto. Kali involves knifework, which Emerson gained expertise in. In 1979 Emerson, dissatisfied with combat knives available at the time—they were primarily fixed-blade designs, which are bulky to carry—resolved to create effective combat knives that could fold. With a background in precision machining, he was well suited to the task. Emerson's knife-making was a hobby—evenings, weekends—until he attended the Pasadena Gun Show. There he learned there was an ecosystem of custom knife manufacturers, and that he could actually make his hobby his living. Before long Hughes had lost an employee, and Emerson transitioned to knife-making full time. As his combat knives developed a reputation, Hughes was approached by members of a Navy SEAL team, who asked him to design a close-quarters combat knife for them. Emerson agreed, adding an unusual

https://www.core77.com/posts/145501/Saud.summary: For a while now, Saudi Arabia has been seeking to pivot away from fossil fuels as their main source of revenue. Even so, I did not see this coming. Ceer is a new Saudi Arabian auto manufacturer, the country's first. And they're going to produce vehicles that don't even run on the petroleum the company is known for producing. Their inaugural model is the Exobot, an EV that will come in both sedan and SUV flavors. Giorgetto Giugiaro would've loved these wedges: These are high-performance (850 horsepower) vehicles with gigantic windshields, another thing I wouldn't have expected from a country with punishing sunlight. The vehicles' air conditioning units are said to be particularly robust, having been designed specifically for the Saudi Arabian climate; the company says they can get the cabin temperature down from 149°F to 90°F (65°C to 32°C) in 10 minutes. (How crazy is it that 90°F is the target .) The idea is that you'd start the air conditioning via app, before you get into the scorching car. This allows you to store it in a space much smaller than its in-use footprint. The trailers are made primarily from aluminum, with stainless steel hardware and a steel axle. They come in multiple sizes, ranging from 4x8 to 6x12, with cargo capacities ranging from 2,122 lbs to 2,312 lbs. These are produced by Canadian company Apogee Trailers , and run roughly $4,500 to $6,500.

https://www.core77.com/posts/145514/A-Mi.summary: 21c Museum Hotels is a hospitality company that combines boutique hotels and restaurants with contemporary art gallery spaces free to the public. Founders Laura Lee Brown and Steve Wilson , both art collectors, want the public to be able to experience art as part of everyday life. Brown and Wilson also have a thing for penguins, which they use as their public-art mascot. Not real penguins; the duo purchased a number of penguin statues made out of recycled plastic, and have populated their six hotels with them. The penguins, which are rotated throughout the properties by staff, may appear in the lobby, the galleries, the elevators, the restaurants, et cetera. Separately, in 2015 artist and industrial designer Daniel Rozin created Penguins Mirror , an installation that used 450 plush toy penguins as black and white pixels. These were used to form one of Rozin's signature mechanical mirrors, where the penguins act as pixels that reflect the viewer's actions. Brown and Wilson eventually caught wind of Rozin's creation, and commissioned a Penguins Mirror for 21c. Here Wilson demonstrates it in action: "I like how it doesn't take itself too seriously. And that's kind of perfect for 21C,"
https://www.core77.com/posts/145514/A-Mi.title: A "Mirror" Made Out of Motorized Penguins

https://www.core77.com/posts/145515/Tita.summary: Here's a fascinating way to travel: Bikerafting. First popularized in Alaska in the 1980s, you ride through the wilderness on your bike, carrying a packraft (an inflatable raft). Image: Kokopelli When you reach a body of water… Image: Kokopelli …you inflate the raft, load up your bike, and cross. Image: Kokopelli Depending on conditions, it can get kind of hairy. Tying your stuff down securely is important, so that nothing gets lost in the drink. Rather than rope, which can get wet, bikerafters traditionally used waterproof, polyurethane ski straps to hold their gear down. Image: Kokopelli In 2010, when preparing for a 300-mile bikerafting trip through Alaska's Lost Coast, adventure photographer Cameron Lawson wanted something more secure. He expanded upon the ski strap, overmolding the buckle with the polyurethane for a sturdier connection. He also beefed up the straps themselves, making them wider and thicker, and adding texture so that they could be grabbed with gloves on. "The straps worked exceptionally well at securing his equipment in the wet, sandy and rough environment," writes Titan Straps , the company Lawson eventually formed. "And their gear didn't budge as he and his
https://www.core77.com/posts/145515/Tita.title: Titan Straps: Fast, Tough Tie-Down Straps Invented for a Bikerafting Trip

https://www.core77.com/posts/145517/Meta.summary: There's a gigantic size gap between VR glasses and ordinary spectacles. I expected Apple to start closing that gap first, but instead it's Meta that's taking the design lead. Their forthcoming Meta VR glasses have chunky stems, but otherwise look a lot closer to regular eyewear. Incredibly, they weigh just 100g (3.5 oz). The Meta Quest 3, their incumbent design, weighs five times as much. The design team achieved the weight savings in two ways: One, while the glasses contain the display, cameras and sensors, they offloaded the battery, storage and processor into a separate puck tethered to the glasses. Two was a materials choice, as Meta industrial designer Mauricio Romano reveals: "The housings are magnesium, a weight-to-strength optimization at this particular scale," writes Romano. "Plastic would need walls too thick, other metals are just too dense. One of the hardest weight puzzles on the whole project." Another trade-off that had to be made was reducing the field-of-view (FOV) from 110° on the Meta Quest 3 to 70° for the new design. Romano explains what went into the decision: "Pixel density, size and weight of actual display, CPU tax, battery tax, how far it sticks out from
https://www.core77.com/posts/145517/Meta.title: Meta's Radically Thinner, More Lightweight VR Glasses

But these days anything goes, with some designers turning the joinery itself into a point of visual interest. A case in point is this 1000L modular storage system: If you're confused by the joinery, the metal supports have not been fancily machined; what you're looking at are angle irons that sit in dual kerfs cut into the uprights at 45°. It's a little more clear if you look at the raw units prior to lacquering: Though a bit odd, t's a low-tech and cost-effective solution. Choosing LFP cells meant a physically larger battery, but the improved safety and longer lifespan was more important for our idea of an everyday vehicle. https://www.core77.com/posts/145531/A-De.summary: If you're into industrial design history, here's a worthwhile destination: The X-D-E-P-O-T , a long-term exhibition by German design museum Die Neue Sammlung at their facility in Munich. What was originally meant to be storage space has instead been filled with 600 notable objects spanning 30 design themes. Many of the objects and content presented in the X-D-E-P-O-T have never before been exhibited. These include objects from the collection segments of tools, packaging design, gaming or secondary architecture, material studies on carbon, wickerwork, metal or industrial ceramics, sample items on the colors red and green, and current topics such as medical design, sustainability or protection. The X-D-E-P-O-T does not structure things by chronology, geographical boundaries or hierarchy. Objects from different periods in time and of different origins and with no traditional canon are presented together for the sake of opening up new angles on them. The focus is on phenomena, high-quality design, and good ideas. Here's a ton of shots from Canadian video producer Isaac Mosna , who calls it "a design wonderland" and "a gallery that proves good product design is art:" And here's video: I
https://www.core77.com/posts/145531/A-De.title: "A Design Wonderland:" The X-D-E-P-O-T, a Repository of Good Design

https://www.core77.com/posts/145538/UTV-.summary: UTVs, or Utility Terrain Vehicles, are popular in rural America. Also called side-by-sides, they're essentially ATVs that can seat two or four people, and some 420,000 were sold in America last year. Farmers, ranchers, rural property owners, and hunters use them. So do individuals and families going on trail-riding vacations. The hunters and trail rider market segments face a challenge, which is that you have to transport the UTV to site. That requires a flatbed trailer. Hooking one of those up means you cannot tow a camping trailer, which for some is a family vacation must-have. Idaho-based Toyup Industries introduced a solution: The Cabover UTV Deck . This is a steel deck that sits in a pickup truck's bed and is secured by connecting turnbuckles to the factory tie-down points; there's no drilling required. Then you attach the two wheel ramps, and you can drive your UTV right up onto your truck: The ramps then stow on top of the rack, but under the UTV. You still have the entirety of the bed available for storage. And, of course, you can then hook up a camper: It's not clear if Toyup Industries invented the idea; they only say they were "the first company in the USA to introduce"

https://www.core77.com/posts/145541/Hell.summary: As a product category, the smartphone is singularly bizarre: You buy it for its convenience, then buy secondary devices that prevent you from using it. As if you, the user, have no willpower. The Brick and Unpluq tags on the market will block certain apps, since you cannot be trusted to not access them; Yondr bags are used by venues that cannot trust you to turn your phone off. Well, here's yet another piece of plastic and circuits you can buy, to avoid having to develop willpower. The Picco , by Chinese manufacturer Boox, is a separate e-reader screen that attaches to the back of your phone. It then allows you to read e-books, which you could simply do by using the regular screen on your phone. Oh wait a second, no you can't, because of the whole willpower thing. So yes, spend $100 on this additional object that you'll also have to keep charged. Can you think of any other product category that has spawned a secondary category of objects designed to prevent you from accessing the original thing? The only thing I can think of are those flip-up button and switch covers, or maybe those breathalyzer ignition interlocks.
https://www.core77.com/posts/145541/Hell.title: Hell in a Handbasket: An Add-On Reading Screen for Your Phone So You Don't Have to Develop Willpower

https://www.core77.com/posts/145547/In-a.summary: Spanish architects Mireia Luzárraga and Alejandro Muiño, a/k/a TAKK, have made their family home in a former industrial space in Barcelona. At 400 square meters (4,306 square feet), the space is huge, which brought challenges: "It became clear that it would be impossible to climate control the entire space without incurring significant economic and ecological costs," the designers say. They've addressed this in part by designing their daughter's bedroom as a freestanding structure with its own insulation—and they built it out of leftover parts from other projects: CMU blocks, wood, drywall, recycled insulation and wool are all incorporated. So too are what appear to be cabinet jacks. Two sleeping spaces are provided, a breezier one up top for warmer months, and an enclosed space below for warmer months. The entire structure is up on wheels and can be moved around within the larger space. And having left all of the fasteners exposed, the structure can be disassembled and its components reused when their daughter eventually outgrows it.

https://www.core77.com/posts/145562/The-.summary: Putting gasoline into most vehicles is easy—at the pump. The nozzle goes into the filler neck, you pull the trigger. Take away the pump, and it gets considerably trickier. Dirt bikes, tractors and construction equipment must be filled with gasoline or diesel in the field, from portable containers, and the filler necks are often in highly inconvenient location. The filler necks on tractors, for instance, are often in the center of the hood: To fill it, you need to lug a five-gallon gas can up onto the operator's platform, then lean forward and hold the can out in front of you to pour. Five gallons of diesel is heavy and takes a lot of time to pour it. It's easy, as your arms tire, to spill fuel all over the place. One solution is to raise the tractor's loader arms so that they're parallel with the ground, then lay a 2x4 across them on which to rest the gas can. Another solution, which many tractor owners invest in, is to buy a battery-powered pump that allows you to leave the gas can on the ground and run the fuel up through a tube. However, that's a lot of trouble to go to, just to fuel the vehicle. So Tuff Jug , an Idaho-based gas can manufacturer, designed a better solution for t
https://www.core77.com/posts/145562/The-.title: The Tuff Jug Ripper Cap Solves a Tricky Fueling Situation

https://www.core77.com/posts/145566/A-Su.summary: When you think of the classic Swiss Army Knife, you likely envision the common 91mm version. That's the size that became the standard in the 1950s. As ubiquitous as this line is, the strange thing is that Victorinox never updated them with clips, which became popular with other folding knives starting in the 1980s. So if you've got a 91mm SAK, you either fish for it in a pocket, or attach a lanyard to its key ring. Now Tortoise Gear, a licensed accessory maker for Victorinox, is rectifying the omission. Their Lamprey91 is an add-on clip that you can install without disassembling the knife. The clip slides into the thin seam between the handle and internal metal liner, than seats around one of the knife's concealed rivets. Here inventor and Tortoise Gear founder Eric McCormick demonstrates how to install it: That's an impressive piece of remedial design! The Lamprey91 has been successfully Kickstarted, with 23 days left to pledge at press time. They run $25 and are expected to ship in February.
https://www.core77.com/posts/145566/A-Su.title: A Super-Easy-to-Install Add-On Clip for Swiss Army Knives

https://www.core77.com/posts/145571/Indu.summary: There's something pleasingly M.C.-Escher-esque about this Ciclo desk organizer. Spanish industrial designer Eduardo Blanco explains its origin: I needed a pencil holder and I wanted it to have a sculptural look. Something that is always visible on a desk cannot be banal. I also wanted it to give me more options for classification and order among my tools than a normal pencil holder. The result is this: three cylinders repeated around the same axis, stacked and joined one on top of the other. A geometrically quite perfect shape that allows you to organize your desk in an original way, breaking the monotony of classic pencil holders. Blanco 3D-printed the prototypes with the intent of eventually going with injection molding. However, he's also worked up these versions through Open Design Editions, a sort of design incubator run by Barcelona-based design firm Lagranja: Am I crazy, or is that glazed ceramic? Whatever they are, I think the pieces look great with the chunkier wall thickness.

https://www.core77.com/posts/145574/A-Si.summary: This Handy furniture piece is by Taiwanese industrial designer Hsinhung Chou . It's such a simple and useful form factor that I'm surprised I haven't seen it before; I think it'd be useful for everything from gardening to picknicking to household chores and handyman jobs. When I'm outdoors on my property, for instance, I often wish I had a way to carry tools that also offered a table-height surface to work on whatever component I'm repairing. Chou developed the design in reaction to living with an urban balcony, where he had a desire for useful furniture within limited room. "Objects never exist alone in a space," Chou says. "The form of furniture is, in essence, a response to a particular way of living." Thus far it's just a concept, though Chou says he's open to finding a production partner.

https://www.core77.com/posts/145575/A-Ba.summary: This wonderful, Bauhausian Bazar coat rack is by German industrial designer Steffen Kehrle. By transforming the tree into a wire cylinder, Kehrle provides hanging space on the outside, while the interior becomes usable storage space thanks to circular shelves. The shelves can be placed wherever there's a hoop; it's up to the user. My only gripe is that I wish it came with more hooks that the user could place. https://www.core77.com/posts/145578/User.summary: Reading a book is very different from studying a textbook. With the former, you flip through pages at whatever pace you read. With the latter, you leave the textbook open to a particular page while you take notes, transcribe, or re-read text in order for it to sink in. For this latter situation, Japanese stationery company Kokuyo detected a problem. In 2022, the company sought feedback from junior high and high school students on what their study-time paint points were. The students noted that holding a textbook open with one hand while trying to write with the other was a hassle. Some used spring-loaded clips made for the purpose, but these made turning the pages a hassle. Others compensated by using a bunchin , a traditional calligraphy scroll weight that's essentially a piece of bar stock, square in cross section. But the flat bunchin didn't hold the books open well, as the flat shape only contacted the curved surface of the open pages in two places. Kokuyo then devised this object, made out of brass. https://www.core77.com/posts/145585/Etto.summary: Ever since the Anglepoise lamp's introduction in 1933 , desk lamps typically cantilevered the light source outwards from the base. Roughly four decades later, Ettore Sottsass threw this convention out with his irreverent Valigia desk lamp. There is no counterweighted base, just four legs that support the lamp head as if it's a tabletop. The form demands commitment, sitting directly above whatever you're reading. Sottsass added a handle at the top, envisioning this as an object you'd carry from place to place. ("Valigia" is Italian for "suitcase.") It's worth noting that Sottsass designed this in 1977, foreshadowing the Memphis movement by a few years. Here in the 2020s, original manufacturer Stilnovo has brought it back onto the market. But I think they missed a trick: While they've changed the lighting to LED, they failed to add a rechargeable battery as the power source. Had they done that and removed the cord, the design would've been closer to what Sottsass would've wanted.

https://www.core77.com/posts/145588/An-I.summary: In the early 1950s, Chicago-based industrial design firm Painter, Teague and Petertil won an interesting commission: Design the world's first portable transistor radio. Texas Instruments had worked out the miniaturization, then partnered with electronics brand Regency to create a consumer product. All they needed was an ID firm to give their technology a consumer-friendly form. The design team got to work, and the Regency TR-1 hit the market in 1954. This was a game-changing device, a predecessor to the Walkman or the iPod. Up until then, families owned a single radio that they'd gather around, like it was a hearth. But now a teenager could take this tiny radio into their room and listen to whatever stations they wanted, or take their music on the go. Regency sold at least 150,000 of these, and competitors wanted in. Raytheon released their 8TP in 1955. It was sleeker in appearance, but considerably larger than the TR-1. In 1957, a Japanese upstart called Sony released their TR-63. In 1960, Zenith released their Royal 50 model. https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1581.summary: 流量依赖症要不得。 首发： 张知愚 01 从公域里获取流量当然没有问题，但是拿到流量之时你是谁呢？ 一个粉丝可以和刘亦菲拍照，这也是一种获得流量的方法，但是有什么真实价值吗？和刘亦菲拍过照片的人何止千万，你的独特之处在哪呢？ 如果没有回答这个问题，任何借势都没有用。 例如雷军是顶流IP。两会上周云杰和雷军并排出现，迅速火出圈。但是前提是他是海尔CEO。很多小米车主都有跟雷军合影的机会，哪个成名了？ 曾经鸿星尔克也火爆一时，但是现在它已经淡出主流，根本原因还是它没有回答这个问题：你到底有何不同。 02 流量会越来越贵，贵到你根本赚不到钱，贵到你几乎是在为流量提供方打工。 举个例子，一个做了十几年的婚纱摄影店，一开始靠门店引流做得挺好，后来发现了互联网买流量也挺好，于是广告不打了，甚至门店也关了，省下钱来买流量。 慢慢就会发现流量费用高到离谱。这时候即使想要开门店做广告也没钱了，企业对流量已经极度依赖，没有额外费用了。 企业已经失去了对流量的主权，只能依赖流量商人的导入。而且流量越来越贵，越来越不好用，但是还没法放弃。 这时候你就被套上了流量枷锁：不买流量马上就死，买流量是慢慢地死。 事实上，得益于大数据和人工智能的技术进步，流量商人——美团、天猫、京东等等——已经可以把流量费用计算到刚好你不会倒闭但也没法赚钱的比例。 03 互联网和移动互联网的革命，给网红品牌提供了远超以往品牌的 流量机会 。在传统品牌还没有反应过来的时候，网红品牌已经迅速成长。 事实上，每一次流量的革命，都是顾客注意力的转移，都会带动一批新的网红品牌。 互联网的出现造就了新浪、搜狐、百度；移动互联网的出现带动了今日头条、微信；从图文到视频的革命出现了优酷、土豆；从长视频到短视频的变化带动了抖音、快手。 淘宝的崛起带动了御泥坊、阿芙精油、韩都衣舍、小狗电器等品牌；天猫也有意识地培养自己平台上的品牌如三顿半、王饱饱、自嗨锅等；小红书的流量辅助了完美日记、元气森林等品牌的成长。 04 也正因为新方式的快捷便利，让很多网红品牌患上了 流量依赖症 。 例如三只松鼠。 章燎原说： “我们凭借价格战优势，进军全品类，在电商的大流量时代三只松鼠的战略就是品类收割。” 所以你定位在生活方式，定位在品类，高端、低端人群，我觉得它本身是定位的一种。 比如像我们三只松鼠这个品牌，你很难说从一而终进行的一种定位，因为当年上线的时候，定位为互联网的坚果品牌，这就是为了要区别于线下一切坚果的品牌，那么实际上走到今天之后，我们是不是一种生活方式？因为我也说不清楚，但是消费者感受到的是，我们能够通过萌萌的形象传递我们的爱和快乐，然后在这个基础上提出我们的核心使命，要让天下人爽起来，这个爽字就会在围绕消费者为中心的这种思维下面。 三只松鼠一开始等于互联网坚果，后来渐渐失去了这个位置，三只松鼠想变成 "爱和欢乐"。 那么问题来了

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1581.summary: 品牌或许依旧强大，但却会流失对催生这个市场的原始需求的主导权。 “品类”，是一个被“实用”绑架的概念。 放到全球商业语境里，它方便写进 “ 业绩报表 ” ，能让公司轻松计算市场份额、识别对手、组合产品线、衡量渗透率、跟踪成果；而在国内，它更是 “ 营销提案 ” 里的常客，“抢占心智×品类第一”火了二十多年，企业家创业者们一听就能上头。 可对于“品牌战略”而言，品类是一个糟糕的起点。 为什么这么说？ 品类本质是供给端的归类方式，把生产、销售同类产品的品牌归在一起。但消费者并不按照这套分类思考，他们只在意自身目标、待解决的问题与所处现实的场景。考量的备选方案，往往会跨越多个品类。 当 “ 需求的满足方式 ” 发生改变时，这一差异就至关重要。品牌或许在自己的品类里依旧强大，但却会悄悄流失对 催生这个市场的原始需求的主导权。 耐克、妮维雅、谷歌，就是同一困境下的三个故事。 三个品牌的知名度、渗透率、渠道铺货，个个是优等生，按品类指标衡量，都属于顶级玩家。但它们被同一个难题卡住： 如果塑造需求的控制点不在原来的位置了，怎么办？ 在细谈三个品牌之前，我们先简单了解两个概念—— “需求空间”与“控制点”。 一、从需求出发，而非品类 当公司透过现有产品、业务单元和品类去看市场时，它会自带“盲点”。需求优先与增长模型的第一步，是绘制“消费者需求生态系统”。 ——埃里克·乔基姆塞勒博士 早在二十年前，品牌大师埃里克・乔基姆塞勒博士便提出一个主张： 增长要立足于需求，而非产品、品类或是传统的市场细分。 思考的起点，是人们真实的生活方式，是他们日常的行动、遇到的难题、身处的场景，还有不断变化的行为。他将这套观察所得的整体图景 命名为 需求图景 （demand landscape）。 这不是概念包装，也不是营销噱头。 苹果是最好的例证。索尼把市场定义为 “便携音乐播放器” ，一心琢磨怎么造出更好的随身听； 苹果着眼的却是音乐背后整条需求链—— 人们如何发现音乐、获取音乐、整理音乐、携带音乐、聆听音乐。 同一个市场，不同的角度，机遇完全不同。 再看两个例子。 用户离开百度，并非出现性能更强的搜索引擎，而是小红书、抖音带来的“边刷边找”的乐趣。 小龙虾、鸭脖这类餐饮消费下滑，也并非是价格变动，而是大家舍不得把玩手机的时间腾给剥壳和啃骨头。 今天，乔基姆塞勒把这类需求的聚集场域称为 “需求空间"（demand spaces）” 。它可以是一项诉求，一个场景，一段生活片段，或是想要达成的目标。企业要把品牌资源和资本投向各类需求空间，而不是死守现有品类划定的竞争边界。 简单来说， 品类讲的是企业当下如何组织供给，而需求空间，反映用户真正想要实现什么。 二者重合时，品类分析还有用，一旦错位，品类思维变成画地为牢。 二、控制点：需求在哪里被塑造？ 2022年，乔基姆塞勒在新书《交互场域》中谈到，企

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1583.summary: 品牌真正值钱的东西，反而都很朴素。 这几年品牌只要改slogan，一般都是往上升华。 产品讲过了，就升华成生活方式。 生活方式讲过了，就升华成情感。 情感再往上，就升华成态度、价值观、社会意义。 这个操作大家都很熟悉了。 但最近我发现，有些品牌居然开始把slogan往回改—— 从情感价值，回落到购买理由； 从大情绪，回落到产品体验； 从大价值，回落到只有自己能占的价值； 甚至从社会意义，回落到产品本身该做的事。 我暂且把这种现象叫作： 品牌价值回落。 这里的“回落”不降级。更像是品牌发现，价值说得太大、太远之后，反而越来越难回答他们的消费者几个最基本的问题： 你到底好在哪？ 为什么我要买你？ 为什么非得是你？ 问题不在升华，问题在于我们很容易把“往上走”当成品牌发展的唯一方向。 下面这些例子，你会看到，这些品牌是怎么在slogan上倒退的？ （注意，下面这些有些是真的改回老slogan，有些只是把表达重新往产品、购买理由上收） 1、京东、John Lewis、大众点评： 从情感价值，回落到购买理由 例1·京东 2013年：多·快·好·省 2015年：只为品质生活 2020年：不负每一份热爱 2023年：多·快·好·省 京东前几次广告语变化，其实一直在往上走。 “多快好省”讲的是最直接的零售利益，“只为品质生活”从购物效率走向生活方式； 再到“不负每一份热爱”，则进一步进入情感价值。 看起来，这是一条都能写进教科书里的路径： 功能 → 品质生活 → 情感价值，一路升维。 三年后，随着低价竞争越来越激烈，刘强东重新把“低价”提到战略核心，“多快好省”也重新高频出现。 “不负每一份热爱”，听起来挺高级的，可是很难回应消费者觉得京东贵了，不值了。（至少我个人而言，已经很久不在京东买东西了） 所以“多快好省”的回归，不只是换回一句旧广告语，还是在重新回答， 为什么还要在京东买？ 例2·John Lewis百货 1925年：Never Knowingly Undersold 绝不有意让你买贵 2022年：For All Life’s Moments 陪伴人生每一个时刻 2024年：Never Knowingly Undersold 绝不有意让你买贵 这句老话讲得很直接，在 John Lewis 买，不用担心自己买贵。 2022年，因为旧的价格承诺越来越难适应电商竞争，John Lewis 顺势做了一次品牌升级，从“价格”走到“人生陪伴”。 但更现实的问题一直没消失，消费者对它的“值不值”并没有那么清楚。 于是2024年，它重新启用原来的价格承诺，并同步升级比价机制，监测25家主要竞争者的价格，发现更低价就跟价。 这句老话重新回来，说到底还是一句： 别让我买贵。 陪伴人生可以加分，但价格公道才是下单理由。 例3·大众点评： 早期：吃喝玩乐，找优惠 2016年：发现品质生活

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1584.summary: 当文化资本不再稀缺，消费者还愿意支付溢价吗？ 原标题：Aēsop如何制造「慢欲望」？ 前段时间，实验犬公益机构“比格公社”发表了一封公开感谢信给护肤品牌Aesop（伊索）。 起因是，Aesop在全国多家门店推出 “爪爪会客厅” 活动，邀请用户携爱犬做客，领取宠物饼干礼，体验清洁服务，并将宠物清洁露销售额的5%捐给比格公社。 乍看这是一场普通的宠物营销， 但在公开信里，比格公社提到Aesop此次合作没有任何要求，纯粹只想捐助实验犬。 我关注Aesop这个品牌很多年，它其实做了不少像这样“格格不入”的事。 从各种影像展览、三八节送书，到文学图书馆、宠物公益，还有像散文一般的推送文案、时不时的歌单分享， 这些事都不会刺激消费者立马下单，但会在他们心里埋下一颗种子，等某个时机才悄悄发芽。 我把这种状态称为 “慢欲望”，不追求即时转化，而是先慢慢发酵品牌认同。 正如创始人Dennis Paphitis所说， 好的产品应该慢慢显现，如耳语而非呐喊，直到它成为你个人世界的一部分。 在当下什么都求快和ROI的商业社会里，这可能也是Aesop最为与众不同的地方。 一、Aesop如何制造「慢欲望」？ Aesop建立“慢欲望”的方式，可以从三个维度来看。 首先是用价值观代替卖点。 和朋友们提到Aesop，我们的主要印象其实都不在具体某款产品上， 而是它持续输出的一套价值观，关注性别议题，热爱文学与艺术，尊重动物及自然。 女性文学图书馆可以说是最典型的案例之一。 2023年三八妇女节，Aesop上海东平路门店的产品全部换成了女性主题的书籍。据报道，店内共41种书目、超过1万册，顾客无需消费，就能免费带走一本书和一个帆布袋。这些书都是全价采购自远方书屋、乐开书店、梯书店、半层书店四家上海本地独立书店，此举也为了支持实体书店的发展。 点击查看项目详情 2024年，同样的活动以“ 双城记 ” 为主题，扩展至上海和广州三家门店，总书量达2.3万册，覆盖51部作品。 而最近，女性文学图书馆再度启程，先后在重庆北城天街、武汉武商Mall和武汉SKP落地。 虽然门店在活动期间几乎无法产生销售收入，但品牌借此与消费者成了一次更深的情感连接。“爪爪会客厅”的宠物公益也是如此， 比起卖出的宠物清洁露，更重要的是传递品牌关爱动物、拒绝动物实验的价值主张，从而积累起消费者的好感度。 用门店空间制造体验记忆，是建立“慢欲望”的第二重维度。 Aesop门店的特别之处在于，它是一种品牌理念的实体化表达。Aesop 亚太区总经理Frederic Seiller在接受采访时曾用 “感官（Sensory）”、“人文（human）”、“审慎（considered）” 这三个关键词来描述品牌，而门店也能体现这些特质。 在Aesop的门店里， 这种“感官性”表现为具体的空间体验，从迎接顾客的香气，不同材质带来的触觉， 经过

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1588.summary: 东方树叶是怎么做大的？ 作者：胡一鸣，来源： 一鸣谈品牌 在很多人的认知里，农夫山泉就是一家卖水的公司。 但如果看了农夫山泉最新的财报，你会发现一个反常识的数据：2026年上半年，农夫山泉的茶饮料卖了131.2亿，而水只卖了96.4亿，茶饮料比水多卖了35亿。 茶饮料进一步取代水，成为农夫山泉的第一大业务。而这背后的头号功臣，就是东方树叶。 这就引出了一个很违背直觉的问题： 一个靠包装水打下江山的企业，为什么允许另一个品牌抢走自己核心业务的主位？ 很多企业也想要打造第二增长曲线，但在战略资源的投入上却出现错配，生怕被新业务抢了风头。 东方树叶反超农夫山泉说明了一件事： 一个企业真正的战略能力，不是靠死守原来的第一业务，而是主动培养出一个能够超越原业务的新增长引擎。 这篇文章，我们就来拆解一下，农夫山泉是如何克服“老业务包袱”，把新引擎做大的？ （图片来源：网络公开资料） 01. 企业最大的增长障碍，往往是过去的成功 很多企业通常不是看不到新机会，而是舍不得重新分配资源。 人在决策时容易陷入 “损失厌恶” 。对企业而言，把资源砸给一个看不清未来的新业务，带来的心理痛苦远大于守住基本盘的踏实感。 包装水曾经是农夫山泉绝对的核心业务。 回到2019年，包装水收入占比接近60%，而茶饮料只有可怜的13.1%。如果完全按照当时营收规模去切分预算，东方树叶可能就没有机会反超。要知道，东方树叶在2011年刚上市时，市场反馈堪称灾难，甚至常年被消费者打上“难喝”的标签。 当时主流货架全被含糖饮料霸占，无糖茶的消费需求根本没有成熟。 大多数企业遇到这种情况，通常只有两个动作： 一是赶紧停掉低效产品止损；二是向市场妥协，加点糖迎合当下的主流口味。 但农夫山泉选择了坚持。这不是靠盲目硬扛，而是对于趋势的准确判断。 他们认定无糖、健康的即饮茶是必然的结构性方向，当下的遇冷仅仅是因为消费者的习惯还未养成。 这就是我想分享的第一个结论： 战略不是根据今天最大的业务分配未来，而是根据明天的机会配置今天的资源。 不过，你看准了机会，就一定能做成吗？ （图片来源：网络公开资料） 02. 东方树叶的成功，不只是因为看懂趋势 很多企业也看懂了趋势，但是却犯了另一个致命错误：所有产品都用同一个品牌，美其名曰为了省钱。 试想一下，如果当年直接推出“农夫山泉无糖茶”，短期内能省下一些推广费，但这在品牌战略上绝对是一场灾难。 为什么？因为消费者的认知很难改变。在他们的认知里，“农夫山泉”这四个字，早就和天然水、大自然的搬运工绑定。 如果你推“农夫山泉无糖茶”，消费者的潜意识就会觉得，你做茶可能不太专业。 因此，农夫山泉必须为这个新品类建立“东方树叶”这一独立品牌。 它的名字、包装、视觉表达，全都在服务于“茶饮料”的认知，绝不迁就包装水的资产。 但在消费者看不见的后台，东方树叶又充分利用了农夫山泉的既有资

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1588.summary: 网友点火，品牌添柴。 原标题：海尔误上颁奖台、雪王闯进月饼圈，这届网友才是最强乙方吧 有些网友的营销天赋，恐怕在在座各位广告人、正规军之上。 以前大家总觉得，创意必须出自高大上的 4A 会议室，必须经过层层审批和精雕细琢，be like《早春晴朗》。 现在的真实情况是， 这届网友意外成了地表最强乙方，不用过五关斩六将的提案，偶然的一条评论、一条帖子、一条视频都有可能成为品牌的爆款创意。 「网友点火，品牌添柴」 的共创模式，正在成为品牌营销性价比最高（but 也是最不可控）的妙计。 海尔“返聘”1997年洗碗机 被网友连夜要求量产 最近，海尔的一台三十年前的洗碗机“翻红”了。 事情的起因是一位小红书博主@虾球多看书曾在去年分享过自己二十多年前的洗碗机非常好用，没有智能化电子屏，一小时连洗带干燥碗底都在发光，复古老式的外观造型让人无法抗拒，完全是博主的梦中情机。 当时的评论区大多还是在感慨二十年前就有这种好东西了。 这其实是海尔第一代台式洗碗机「小海贝」，1997 年出厂的。博主甚至前前后后购入了四次这台洗碗机，足以看出此人对海尔的喜爱程度了，海尔老式洗碗机重度依赖。 但在今年 3 月份，这台洗碗机莫名其妙地坏了，指示灯乱闪，蜂鸣器乱叫，一合上盖子就无法运作。 博主只是发此帖表达一下对“已逝”洗碗机的惋惜心痛之情，但没想到海尔官方客服真的在评论区留言反馈了，只是博主认为型号太老旧，机器配件停产修不好了。 故事到这里，应该只是一台老家电寿终正寝的 normal ending。然而命运的齿轮开始转动了，一直到今年8月，还有源源不断的网友在问这台洗碗机的购买意见，以至于博主又发了一条关于洗碗机的“种草”视频。 但这并非红稿一篇！ 前半段博主用尽赞美之词，“它的外形、它的容量、它的这种运作方式、带烘干的功能、20 来分钟的洗涤时长，还有这种摆放方式，真的可以称得上完美”，简直快要把海尔哄成胚胎了。 后半段态度大转弯， 又用最直接、最残忍、最不绕弯子的话企图劝退想要购买同款的网友们：“不建议大家购入的，因为它 100% 会漏水，而且后续出问题的话，也不会有任何的解决方案。” 博主这条纯为爱发电的视频也引起了一些网友们的关注，“ 厂家：看到前半段，想着这个铁粉要不要送她台新的，看到后半段，等等。 ” “如果不是博主，我都不知道还有这种样式的洗碗机。” 而它的名字「小海贝」也同样可爱，让人感觉到了海尔的工程师也很爱这款产品。 海尔初代洗碗机并没有电子屏，没有过于复杂的功能，这样一台老式洗碗机也让网友们意识到“家电行业近十几年增加的是触控屏和智能化，实际功能其实没有质的飞跃。” 这条视频劝没劝退网友不好说，但确实把海尔官方给“劝”过来了，毕竟那句“不会有任何的解决方案”怎么不算是激将法呢？ 海尔在帖子还没完全热出圈时就已经先一步私信博主，表明这台「小海贝」对海尔来说也是意义非凡

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1588.summary: 猎奇酸奶的口味有多超前？ 来源： 硬壳INK 上一代人出门旅游，背回来特产多少和当地沾点关系。 去新疆带葡萄干，去云南带鲜花饼，几乎是一种约定俗成。 但现在的年轻人不一样了，各地猎奇口味的酸奶，成了一种很新的伴手礼。 把时间往回倒，老酸奶曾经也当过一阵城市名片，相似的瓷瓶包装统一的怀旧字体，无论去哪个城市喝起来都是一样噎人。 如今的酸奶研发突然进入白热化，酸奶厂商开始放飞自我。 大家像是有什么秘密约定，有什么好东西都全都加进酸奶里。 于是，西安有了油泼辣子酸奶，贵阳开发出折耳根、木姜子、花椒的猎奇口味，济南干脆把把子肉塞进了酸奶。 图/小红书用户@馋馋的奇食记 酸奶不是酸奶了，更像一种披萨、一种底座，堆上各种激进新口味。 为什么奇奇怪怪味道都被放在了酸奶里？ 一、猎奇酸奶的口味有多超前？ 曾几何时超市货架上的酸奶原本是主打减法，什么健康配方，0糖添加。 后来普通口味酸奶没法满足人类的好奇心。 开始只是常规口味尝试，继果味之后研究出果粒、燕麦、咖啡、酒酿的创新组合。 后来， 辣椒 来了，再后来 折耳根、花椒、木姜子 也被加入酸奶。 没人再关心配料表有几行，谁的口味猎奇谁就是酸奶之王。 口味创新根本没有天花板，当把子肉酸奶出现，酸奶就已经不满足于充当饭后甜品，开始有点想独立完成一顿正餐。 贵阳的折耳根酸奶 ，把这场口味实验拉到了另一个层面。 折耳根原本就是一种地域分界线极强的食物。 喜欢的人恨不得顿顿拿它拌蘸水，不喜欢的人光听见名字就开始干呕。 有网友喝完留言折耳根酸奶清新上头。 让人很难不怀疑，这是不是贵州人对外地游客发动的一场服从性测试。 以前外地人想认识贵州风味，得先吃酸汤、烙锅和各种蘸水。 现在不用了，一排酸奶喝过去，就能完成一次青春版舌尖贵州行。 网友也顺着这条思路继续在酸奶里点菜，章丘大葱、糖醋鲤鱼也没落下。 后来确章丘大葱实被做成了酸奶口味，成功弥补了上班不方便吃大葱的遗憾。 兰州把浆水变成酸奶，天津海河把煎饼果子从固体变成液体。 到了这里，问题已经不再是酸奶适合和什么搭。 而是还有什么味道，没有被酸奶厂商发现。 真正版本领先的酸奶来自湛江。 研发团队将沙虫和生蚝成分加入发酵乳体系，试图做出具有海洋特色的酸奶。 有喝过的网友评价：沙虫酸奶让人想到电影《沙丘》。 生蚝酸奶则成功让生蚝爱好者和酸奶爱好者一起陷入沉默。 酸奶口味走向猎奇之后，网上的信息也变得虚实难辨。 图/AI酸奶图 很多网友会自己用AI生成的包装概念图玩梗。 手搓一款不存在的酸奶，成了一种互联网抽象整活。 知了猴酸奶、豆汁酸奶都是AI生成的。 对很多酸奶生产商来说，AI生图的口味也变成一种流量验证。 评论区提创意，品牌负责接单，社交媒体检验爆款潜力，猎奇酸奶也成了大家的一个大型互联网众筹项目。 图/小红书用户@奶牛小哞 二、酸奶为什么适合爆改？ 每隔一段时间，身边都会自动刷新出流行的零

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1588.summary: 下一阶段酒品牌争夺的，也许不是更多喝酒场景，而是新的喝酒理由。 原标题：酒在，江湖在，人换了 当酒品牌都开始走进生活，下一步争的可能不是更多场景，而是喝酒的理由。 大伙习惯说一句：“有空聚聚，小酌一下。” 有意思的是，我们真正想说的，往往不只是那杯酒。 可能是很久没见了，想聚一下； 可能是有些话平时不好说，到了桌上才容易开口； 也可能是什么重要的事都没有，只是觉得两个人应该见一面。 酒在中国人的生活里，从来不只是酒。它参与过团圆、庆祝、送别、生意、友情等许多时刻，也参与过很多说不清楚的关系。 酒还在，只是坐在桌边的人正在变化。 一、仪式没有消失，只是在寻找新的表达 今天谈酒类消费，很容易谈到年轻人、消费变化、低度化、健康意识等趋势。但这些变化背后，还有一个更值得品牌关注的问题： 人们为什么喝酒，也在变化。 春节还是要团圆，重要的日子仍然要庆祝，朋友很久不见还是会说“喝一杯”，礼赠、宴请、商务等场合也仍然有酒的位置。很多仪式没有消失，只是人们开始重新判断，自己愿意用什么方式完成它。过去需要一桌人完成的聚会，今天可能只是三两好友；过去习惯用价格和排场表达的关系，也可能转向更轻、更自在的方式。 所谓消费变化，并不意味着情感也跟着降级。真正值得酒品牌追问的是： 当人们不再愿意为过去的排场付那么多钱，他们还愿意为什么付钱？ 而且改变的不只是年轻人。二十岁的时候，酒常常是向外喝的；到了四十岁、五十岁，工作、家庭、得到与失去已经构成了自己的故事，身体也开始提醒自己少喝一点。这个时候， 岁月本身已经是一壶很浓的酒。 年轻时可能需要酒把自己打开，后来可能只需要一杯酒，让自己慢下来。 变的不只是喝多少，而是为什么喝。 二、同一个人，开始拥有很多种喝酒身份 过去我们习惯按照年龄、收入、城市、品类等寻找消费者。 但今天真实的饮酒生活，可能比这些标签复杂得多。 同一个人，商务宴请可能喝白酒，和朋友见面可能选择威士忌等烈酒，旅行时喝啤酒，回到家也可能什么都不喝。即使都是白酒，也有浓香、酱香、清香等不同香型与产品选择；威士忌有不同类型、桶陈与风味表达，精酿啤酒也让更多人开始谈论酒花、麦芽与具体风味。 酒的选择变多了，喝酒的语言也在变多 。 不同的酒，不一定是谁简单替代了谁，更可能是在进入同一个人不同的情绪、关系和人生时刻。 所以酒品牌过去非常熟悉的问题：“我的消费者是谁？”，可能还需要再往前一步： “ 我的品牌，为什么会在他的某一个时刻被需要？” 前一个问题容易把人固定成一种身份，后一个问题开始看见一个人在不同关系、生活阶段和场景里的变化。酒类品牌竞争的，也许不再只是某一种“目标人群”，而是进入一个人有限的饮酒时刻，以及进入那个时刻的理由。 三、当品牌都开始进入生活，下一步争什么？ 酒品牌其实早已意识到生活正在变化。从近期不少白酒品牌的内容来看，历史、产区、工艺、品质、香型等传统价值仍然

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1589.summary: 你钱多、奢侈、会享受。 作者：张倍嘉，来源： 远川研究所 郭敬明的《小时代》里，林萧在时尚杂志实习，因为穿了一双三叶草球鞋，被客户当着老板的面讥讽， “你可以多发她一点钱，让她买双像样一点的鞋子么？” 林萧当场落泪，这双三叶草可是简溪在淮海路上adidas旗舰店门口排了三个小时的队，才买到的限量款。但 “在上海时尚圈里，球鞋永远敌不过细高跟鞋。” 如果故事发生在2026年，林萧可以骄傲地挺起头，回呛一声你懂个屁。 她最时尚的朋友顾里，应该早就脱下Gucci小短靴，穿上了从美国比弗利原装进口的alo了。 不久前，预热了几百年的alo终于进入中国，天猫上线1分钟就卖爆1千万，最畅销的SUIT UP直筒裤售价1150元，销量超过1万条。 alo主营业务瑜伽服，和lululemon是一个赛道的，但享受的不是一个待遇。 美国媒体把《American Housewife》描述成“一群穿Lululemon的0码富裕主妇”社区，Lululemon和星巴克成了中产妈妈的标配。 穿着lululemon好像在说我要去接个孩子，顺便上个瑜伽课，而alo则是刚从普拉提教室出来，要带着果蔬汁去沙滩边冥想，后者显然对应着一种不一样的、更贵的生活。 这可能就是 它质量不如lululemon，但卖得lululemon贵 的原因吧。 01 街拍也是一种运动 2007年lululemon上市，成功开辟了瑜伽裤这个细分市场，把小众场景的技术服装变成日常穿着，启发了无数运动服饰领域的同行，其中就包括alo的创始人Danny Harris和Marco DeGeorge。 同年，两人创办alo，取自空气/air、陆地/land、海洋/ocean之意，打着绿水青山的旗号，摸着lululemon过河，主攻瑜伽裤。 这时候，专业和业余的差距就体现出来了。lululemon创始人Chip Wilson是个玩铁人三项的肌肉猛男，alo的两个创始人只是“练过瑜伽”，公司成立近十年都不温不火，口号也是土纯风的“bringing yoga to the world”。 直到2016年，alo发现了一个比瑜伽更广阔的市场： 街拍 。 2016年1月，美国女星肯豆（Kendall Jenner）被拍到穿Alo瑜伽裤逛街，此后，不断有明星穿着Alo瑜伽裤的照片“意外”曝光，终于在2016年8月引起了时尚杂志Teen Vogue的注意，标题很直接[1]： Taylor Swift, Hailey Baldwin, Gigi, and Bella Hadid Wear Alo Yoga Moto Leggings。 穿的同一条Moto Leggings Kendall Jenner、Bella Hadid后来成功拿到alo代言 往事暗沉不可追，来日之路光明灿烂，alo决定抛弃 the best yoga clothing ，变身

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1589.summary: 妥妥的新版《超级变变变》。 首发： 日本设计小站 原标题：笑不活了！韩国博物馆办了场“文物cos大赛”，低成本高还原！网友：新版超级变变变 文物：活了，又好像没完全活 韩国整了个文物cos大赛，真是离谱又还原！ 就在前几天，韩国国立博物馆办了一场 “文物变装” ，趣味程度直接拉满！ 参赛者从博物馆收藏的文物中寻找目标，然后自制服装道具，从头到脚1:1复刻。 把自己活生生“变成”文物本人。 有人扮敲钟的木槌、有人扮金玺、有人扮铜器…… 甚至还有人干脆整个躺在地上，变成一只会打挺的“白瓷鱼形砚滴”。 而且还不是单纯的换装摆拍！ 每位参赛者都要提前设计剧情、编排表演， 用肢体动作生动还原文物的形态和独特神韵。 这不妥妥的新版《超级变变变》吗！ 今年大赛 275支队伍、643人参加，最后只有25支杀进决赛！ 而大奖得主就是那只会鲤鱼打挺的“砚滴”！ 模仿者是一位22岁的大学生。 一身白色连体衣，把头、脸、以及四肢全部涂成蓝色，躯干部分画上鱼鳞。 然后仰面躺下，把手臂当作鱼鳍，抬起双腿，用脚摆出鱼尾扑腾的姿势。 就开启了一连串灵活翻滚、甩尾、弹跳的表演！ 评委给出的夺冠理由是： 别人都在还原“文物的样子”，只有她演活了文物的精气神～ 不过说实话，抛开神韵看外形，不少作品都算是高度还原了！ 比如这件“倚坐造型佛像”。 选手用环形补光灯打造佛像背后的光环，全程靠双脚控制底座缓慢自转。 完美复刻了一腿叠膝、手指轻触脸颊、闭目沉思的经典禅意姿态。 还有人用烧烤店排气罩和大纸箱喷金漆制作了一枚巨大的“金玺”。 甚至还有“纹香炉”、“双狮石灯”、“金铜大香炉”、“佛塔”这些难度较高的模仿，也是手艺和脑洞双双在线。 据说决赛当天有3000多名观众围观，就是为了看一群人一本正经地“演”文物！ 最有意思的是各位参与者赛后感言： 在学习如何装扮成文物的过程中，没有压力，甚至有一丝放松和解压？ 不得不说，人类五花八门的脑洞、松弛的精神状态，真的是ai替代不了的！ 那么，你觉得那个“鲤鱼打挺式”夺冠，值不值第一名呢？ 作者公众号：日本设计小站（ID：japandesign） 更多精彩内容请访问 数英网 - 文章频道 - 项目频道 - 招聘频道

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1589.summary: 未来优秀的购物中心会越来越像一个消费内容平台。 作者/编辑：晓虎，来源： Mall先生 最近，因为做人物访谈以及白皮书的缘故，我们和大量品牌的创始人、拓展负责人聊了聊，问他们怎么选商场，又希望商场为品牌做些什么。 聊的过程中，我发现一些熟悉的经验正在变得不够用，而他们的回答中也传递着一种共同的方向： 今天品牌在开店的过程中，有关商场的选择指标，以及对于好商场的评价和期待，开始有了新的侧重。 于是有了这篇文章。 01 客流之外，更关心空间氛围和客户体验 过去，商户评估一个商业项目，有一套相对成熟的方法 ——看区位、画商圈、数人头、看品牌组合……再叠加租金、面积和具体落位，基本就可以决定一个项目是否进入候选清单。 所以我们大部分项目的招商手册，也离不开这些基础参数的展示。而几乎每个BD手里，也都会装若干个XX猎手之类的大数据小工具。 但当越来越多线下门店不只承担交易功能时， 大家观察的数据和维度也会变得更细、更多样。 比如我最近聊过的一家新锐香氛品牌， chillmore进入蟠龙新天地，便不是一个完全符合传统模型的选择。 且悠chillmore上海蟠龙新天地门店 它们此前的门店/快闪店，是在苏州万象天地、杭州万象城这样的核心商圈标杆项目。按照创始人团队过去在国际大牌所使用的商业评估模型，不在城市核心片区，餐饮占比较高的蟠龙新天地，并不是首选。但团队最终仍然决定试一次。 除了现场如潮的客流，真正让他们下定决心的，是对项目的感受。 弹街路、石板桥、江南水乡和户外环境，让这里天然具有一种“慢”的氛围，让人放慢速度，更容易进入一种散步、驻足，又或是悠然探索、惬意享受的状态。 这种节奏与品牌所强调的“慢生活”“慢美学”恰好相合。 而门店开业后优异的业绩表现，也证明了这一预判的成功。 在和其他品牌的交流中，我们也看到了相似的判断。 一部分创始人，开始更关注客流的购买力、质量，在现场的停留时间，与自己目标客群的匹配程度—— 总之光靠人多，已经不足够打动他们了。 另一些品牌，则把重心放在了铺位之外的整体生态。 比如攀岩业态，净高、承重等工程条件，交通和可达性等传统因素之外，他们还关心两件事情： 一是能否在运动的“之前和之后”，为自己的顾客提供更舒适的体验： 比如开车和停车是否方便？餐饮是否足够好吃？卫生间是否干净？ 正是这些，构成了购物中心对于那些硬件基础更好的厂房的选址优势，也是一部分购物中心pk掉另一部分的重要原因。 二是这里所营造的生活方式，是不是能和我的目标客群所匹配？ 香蕉攀岩的昊勤分享给我说：他们希望进入的，并不只是一个满足净高要求的物业，更是一个“很好玩的空间”。 顾客可以不止因为攀岩这一件事情而来，还有绿地、宠物和咖啡等构成的吸引力。而聚集在这里的消费者，也有可能成为攀岩的新用户。 香蕉攀岩OCT PARK项目 宠物业态的选址逻辑也类似。 从传统客群画像看，它需

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1589.summary: 到底啥是致敬啊？ 看图说话。 其实我只想弄明白一件事，到底什么叫致敬？ 复制就算致敬？复制不等于抄袭？ 换了自己的产品，就算致敬了？ 一样的结构、镜头、画面，但是加了点料，就不算复制了？ 那我这张图算致敬，还是抄袭？ 实在令人疑惑。 到底啥是致敬啊？ 我也搞不清楚，只能去翻翻史书。学不会创新，看看致敬成功的案例，还不行吗？ 案例一 奔驰 & 捷豹 先看原片。 2013年9月，奔驰为了宣传 稳定性 ，创意是用 鸡的身体可以移动、头部却保持稳定 的生理特征，类比S级的MAGIC BODY CONTROL悬架技术。结尾直接落到“Stability at all times”。 《Chicken》 当时视频大火，三个月后，捷豹复刻了这一创意。 《Jaguar vs. Chicken》 前半段几乎明牌复刻奔驰广告片里的鸡，甚至延续同一套“移动身体、头不动”的演示。随后，一地鸡毛，镜头转到一只豹子身上，鸡去哪了不言而喻。 落版： “Magic Body Control? We prefer cat-like reflexes.” 魔术车身控制？我们更信奉猎豹般的敏捷。 关键是，捷豹官方完全没回避出处，他们公开表示，自己“非常喜欢”Mercedes那支广告，所以想给观众一个“不一样的，捷豹的视角（alternate, Jaguar, point of view）”。 案例二 苹果 & Epic Games 苹果广告借用了乔治·奥威尔《1984》的Big Brother意象：一群人机械地听着大屏幕中的权威讲话，一个运动员模样的女性冲进大厅，将铁锤砸向屏幕。 广告最终宣布Macintosh即将发布，并把Apple放在了“挑战既有权威”的位置。 这支片在1984年全国播出，后来成为广告史上最著名的作品之一。 《1984》 再来看致敬者的操作。 同样的巨大屏幕，同样整齐坐着的人群，同样有人冲进会场，同样向屏幕投掷武器，甚至连最后的文案结构都对应Apple原作。 只不过屏幕里的Big Brother变成了一个苹果头。 《堡垒之夜版〈1984〉》 原因是，2020年，Epic 在《堡垒之夜》iOS 版内置绕过苹果支付的直接付费通道，规避苹果 30% 抽成（苹果税）。苹果立刻将 Fortnite 下架 App Store。Epic 几乎同步提起反垄断诉讼，同时放出这支短片，讽刺“屠龙少年终成恶龙”。 再普及个重要知识点： 法律上，欧美版权体系下，讽刺戏仿（Parody）属于合理使用，允许借用经典作品框架进行批判、反讽；这也是这支短片可以直接拿来攻击苹果，而没有被版权起诉的关键原因。 案例三 John Lewis & 奥乐齐 原片在2015年上线，是英国一年一度现象级圣诞广告。 视频中，小女孩 Lily 用望远镜望向月亮，发现月球表面住着一位孤独独居老人。她拼命挥手、扔纸飞机，都无法和对

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1590.summary: 农夫山泉的文案为何深入人心？ 作者：九算，来源： 品牌战争论 当我们在做咨询时，有企业老板说你们说要保持差异化价值的一致性。 但是你看农夫山泉对外都变了好几次广告语，这其实是一个容易被误读的样本。 因为很多人只看到了文案表达的进化史：从农夫山泉有点甜到大自然的搬运工，再到越往山里去，水质就越好，一步步从感性到理性、从产品到水源地到场景。 这个说法没错，但你从差异化品牌价值的角度来看，你会发现农夫山泉22年干的，根本不是传播表达的改变，而是围绕一个天然水这个差异化品牌价值的五次筑墙： 它从来没换过差异化品牌价值，只把这个价值的证据链，一级一级垒成别人翻不过去的护城河。 差异化品牌价值是什么？是消费者大脑里这个品牌对外承诺的是什么，农夫山泉的差异化品牌价值，从第一天起就是天然。 “有点甜”是天然的味觉暗示；“大自然搬运工”是天然的生产方式；“每一滴水都有它的源头”是天然的地理印证；“什么样的水源孕育什么样的生命”是天然的生态印证；“越往山里去，水质就越好”是天然的稀缺价值。 五句广告语，一个价值，证据链越垒越硬，后来者越抄越难。 这才是农夫山泉真正的品牌管理：不换价值，只把证据一级级筑成墙。 01 价值不动，证据升级：五步筑墙，越筑越深 第一步 上世纪90年代末：“有点甜”用口感暗示天然 同期竞品在卷谁的谁更纯净时，如乐百氏的27层净化，农夫山泉从口感暗示出发，越纯净水越是无味的，那我的天然水“有点甜”代表着我和大家不一样，虽然浅，但够用。 因为一个新品牌首先是让消费者记住你和别人不一样，正如那句话不要鹤立鸡群，离开那群鸡。 第二步 2008年前后：“大自然的搬运工”用生成方式定义天然 这是农夫山泉真正的封神之作，它不是一股劲说我天然，它说我只是把大自然的水搬给你，把品牌从制造商降格成搬运工，反而把天然的可信度推到了极致。竞争对手要模仿，那你的先摒弃你的纯净水生产线，放弃过去多年累积的纯净水品牌资产。 第三步 2015年前后：“每一滴水都有它的源头”用从哪里来印证天然 从我们怎么生产转向我们的水从哪来，开始拍水源地、讲长白山、讲千岛湖，广告从口号变成纪录片。 这一步的证据是地理，天然不再是一句形容，而是一个你可以去、可以看、可以验证的地方。竞争对手要模仿，得真去签约优质水源地、铺管道……不是写个文案喊几嗓子，是需要真金白银砸进去。 第四步 2018年前后："什么样的水源孕育什么样的生命"用为什么好印证天然 好水孕育好生命，水源地栖息的生灵就是天然生态最好的印证。但它不是空讲，铺管道、爬悬崖、工人手冻裂……它讲的是为了保住这口好水，我们付出了什么。当品牌愿意为“为什么好”这个答案付出代价时，好才真正立得住。 第五步 2023年："越往山里去，水质就越好"用稀缺提升天然 最新的这句，很多人以为是回归产品。其实是把整个链条收口到山越高水越好，这不是我们说的，是自然逻辑

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1590.summary: 人物五官如奶油般融化在光里了。 来源： LOGO大师 原标题：《复仇者联盟4》重映海报设计太抽象！网友：甲亢哥来出演了吗？ 近日，《复仇者联盟4：终局之战》宣布将以“加码臻享版”重新回归大银幕， 一个吐槽《复联4》“全员出动”的海报的帖子在社交平台火了。 接下来，让我们一起看看这个海报长啥样！ 一、这张《复联4》海报有点“抽象” 被吐槽的海报长这样 海报里的 钢铁侠、美国队长、黑寡妇等角色全部处于战斗状态， 但人物五官的描绘却有点“放飞自我”，人物五官如奶油般融化在光里了。 尤其是《黑豹》中的奥克耶，脸部细节被画得相当抽象，网友一眼看过去，直接联想到 SPEED“甲亢哥”。 甚至调侃： “需要给speed付肖像使用费的程度” 还有表情包“这给我干哪来了.jpg” 也有觉得 像邓超之前饰演的“拉不拉卡”。 “无人在意的角落里寡姐看一眼也是要圆寂了” 还有网友吐槽 海报里的寡姐， 怎么看都像“俄罗斯娜娜”。 小蜘蛛更是直接被网友点名： “小蜘蛛呢” ，大概是蜘蛛感应到了危险，先跑了hhhh... 就连 绿巨人也没能幸免 ，狰狞的表情有点像便秘了... 还有一位甚至是物理意义上的“没人样”。 网友甚至开始怀疑： “饭制恶搞还是官方整活啊？？” 还有觉得诡异的像AI生成的。 不过，吐槽归吐槽，这张海报实际上是2019年《复仇者联盟4》上映期间，漫威官方陆续发布的一组艺术海报的其中一张。 是 由画师Tom Miatke创作 。他长期与漫威、迪士尼、皮克斯等娱乐公司合作，擅长的是这类偏插画风格的电影宣传物料。 经过网友这一轮“考古”，当年的海报又重新火了一遍。 二、这次重映，又出了哪些海报？ 既然说到《复联4》的海报，就不得不看看这次真正为重映推出的视觉物料。和前面那张“抽象艺术海报”不同， 这次的重映海报明显更强调经典场景、初代复仇者和终局情绪。 首先是 重映主海报 。它并非完全重新设计，而是 在Eileen Steinbach 2019年版剪影海报的基础上进行调整。 画面采用中心对称构图，两侧是深色封闭的走廊，远处则是一片纯白高光出口。初代六位复仇者以剪影形式横向排开，背对着光源走来。 重映版vs原版 熟悉的构图重新出现，也让这张重映海报多了一层“回到原点”的感觉。 除了主海报，这次重映还针对不同影院版本推出了一系列视觉物料。 金属浮雕全员海报 直接把英雄们做成了金属浮雕，密密麻麻的群像几乎铺满整个画面。整体是银灰色金属质感，只有无限手套上的6颗宝石保留了彩色。 emmm……乍一看有点像漫威版“十八铜人”。这么多人挤在一起，你能认出几个？ IMAX 海报 直接复刻《终局之战》经典的传送门集结场景。大量英雄从传送门中出现，形成超大规模群像，重点突出影片最后大战的史诗感。 ScreenX 海报 唯一保留灭霸的版本，黑白基底，仅无限宝石保留彩色，黑白画面里宝石亮色形成视觉

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1590.summary: 这场酒局才刚刚开始。 来源： 食部尚书 一年半从 270家飙到3500家，平均每18天就要干出100家新店。 而在 2025年初，其门店数量才仅为270家， 一年半的时间增长超十倍，月均新增门店200家， 这样的扩张速度可谓是媲美早期的蜜雪冰城了。 福鹿家到底在做鲜啤，还是在复制另一个“ 雪王”？ 一、 突破鲜啤传统消费场景 一定意义上说， 鲜啤福鹿家的成功，在于冲破和重构 “鲜啤精酿”赛道。 重构产品价格带，把低价精酿带进大众市场， 福鹿家延续了一贯的低价策略。其门店价目表显示，产品价格集中在 5.9元至9.9元区间，分为鲜啤、奶啤、果啤、茶啤和“当季限定”等不同品类。 其中，德式小麦鲜啤6.6元/杯，微醺小奶啤9.9元/杯，茉莉青提鲜啤9.9元/杯。 传统精酿酒吧一杯 IPA动辄30元起步，独立精酿品牌一杯要40元以上，而 福鹿家将精酿的价格打到了“一杯奶茶”的水平。 这种定价策略，核心目的不是抢精酿市场的蛋糕，而是 瞄准了便利店里的罐装啤酒和不想喝奶茶的年轻人。 用福鹿家的话说： “10块钱能喝到口感更轻盈、麦香更浓郁的‘现打鲜啤’，那大概率不会再选择那种水啤。” 这就是 “比上不足，比下有余” 的定价策略。 它不跟高端精酿比品质，而是跟水啤比品质； 不跟水啤比价格，而是跟高端精酿比价格。 通过这种交叉锚定，福鹿家给自己创造了一个 “高质平价” 的认知护城河。 但是在鲜啤福鹿家身上，我们看到的不仅是 “卖得便宜”，还有敢卖低价的底气。 告别了传统精酿酒吧动辄上百万的重资产投入，福鹿家把目光锁定了 10到15平米的极限空间。 两台啤酒机，一个大冷柜，连带设备不到6万块钱就能支起一个摊子。 非高峰时段，哪怕只有一个人守着店，也能有条不紊地应付日常客流。 这种用茶饮思维重构卖酒生意的打法，彻底把开店门槛踩在了脚下。 回本周期被极大压缩， “即买即走”的流量逻辑加上极致性价比， 让过路客的转化率达到了顶峰。 相对来说，打酒站的模型更轻，不需要像酒吧那样承担完整堂食和社交空间成本，也不需要像大型餐饮门店那样配置复杂厨房，以灵活选址和快速落地的特点，低投入门槛和较少的人力成本，打酒站成为一个回本周期快且能够良性运转的门店模型。 当然，根据品牌定位和产品特点，即买即饮和复购驱动是鲜啤福鹿家经营核心，因此 门店选址也非常关键。 经过全国超 3500家店的选址经验，鲜啤福鹿家基本锁定了四大场景为门店高效选址模型。 具有稳定客流保障的成熟社区， 高频复购和口碑相传，给复购率提供天然的保障，这更像是一个离消费者很近的 “现打零售终端”，降低人们到店的距离成本，让鲜啤进到更多普通消费者的日常生活半径里。 今年 5月，福鹿家干了一件大事。它 把新疆的加盟通道打开了。 要知道，以前物流成本太高，很多品牌根本不敢去新疆开店，运费比酒还贵。 但现在， 靠着蜜雪在兰州刚刚开放的仓储中心

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1591.summary: 大红色、高密度文案、强视觉冲击，非常扎眼。 原标题：麻辣王子米兰广告：土得务实，还是聪明得鸡贼？ 麻辣王子最近在米兰大教堂附近投放广告，引发了一轮争议。 大红色、高密度文案、强视觉冲击，和米兰大教堂的古典建筑放在一起，确实非常扎眼。 很多人说，这是中国品牌出海的审美翻车。 但我觉得，这件事情其实有两种完全不同的可能，而 这两种可能，恰恰代表了中国企业做营销的两条路。 第一种可能： 作坊式营销，土但务实 这种可能其实没有那么复杂，也是国内某知名策划公司的核心思路： 醒目、吸睛、让消费者记住。 因为辣条是什么？ 它本来就不是啥能和"高端品牌"建立关系的产品，你很难指望消费者因为一条辣条的广告，而产生什么高端、优雅、精致的品牌联想。 那怎么办？ 对一个还没建立广泛知名度的品牌， 别想那么多，先把知名度打起来，再配合渠道铺货，把货卖出去。 从这个角度看，这种大红色、强刺激、远距离就能看到的广告，反而非常务实。 甚至不需要讨论什么国际审美。 消费者一眼看见，记住"麻辣王子"，这就完成了第一步。 此前麻辣王子在深圳火车站等高流量场景投放类似广告，其实也是同一套逻辑。 （图片来自围脖网友：玩车豆豆） 不是为了让广告有多高级，而是为了让消费者记住我。 如果是这个逻辑，我反而觉得没什么好大惊小怪的。 对于一个正在铺渠道、抢认知的食品品牌来说，先活下来、卖出去，比讲品牌哲学重要。 这就是典型的销售型营销，不高级，但可能有效。 我个人不喜欢，但也从来不批评。 第二种可能： 鸡贼式营销，聪明但危险 但还有另外一种可能，有点过分。 品牌知道这种广告在国内会引发争议，特意把它搬到米兰这种具有强烈视觉和文化符号的地方，然后等中国游客拍照、网友吐槽、媒体报道，再在国内找个大号，在某平台上想办法弄个热搜，让品牌出圈儿。 核心目的根本不是做海外市场，不过是海外制造事件，在国内收割流量。 这种玩法确实聪明，甚至很可能比单纯投国内广告划算。 这样的事情，我也搞过。 有一年红牛赞助江苏卫视的节目《最强大脑》，某国内奶企是冠名，红牛是最低一级赞助，为了借这个节目制造传播，我们在五道口放了4块广告牌，以挑战清华大学学生为噱头，然后把事件引导到线上，利用网友的好奇心和参与感放大传播，收割了一拨又一拨流量。 甚至很多网友认为那一年是红牛冠名，导致那家奶企还去江苏卫视要说法。 和麻辣王子的广告引发争议不一样，这个营销事件受到网友和媒体一致好评。 对麻辣王子来说，流量确实收割到了，但争议也留下了，还给中国品牌贴上了“LOW B”的标签。 如果一个品牌为了自己出圈，把"扎眼、土味、违和"变成传播卖点，短期当然可以获得大量注意力。 可长期看，消费者记住的到底是什么？ 是"中国辣条很有特色"，还是"中国品牌到了国外，还是这个趣味"？ 这就是两回事。 最后 这件事儿，我其实不太想讨论"广告到底丑不丑"，也不想简单说中国

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1592.summary: 网友巧施连环计，六神误上断头台。 六神你可真刑啊！ 看到有网友晒出了六神包装上今年新包装上的防伪标，这看着也太亲切了吧？ 辨识度之高，恐怕14亿中国人没有一个人不认识。 瓶身上的钞线纹理、暗纹和立体工艺，看起来有模有样，拿在手里还能摸到明显的凹凸感。好家伙，不仅看起来像，摸起来更像。 这事被网友一发现，一切就有了合理的解释。 原来也有人跟我一样 喜欢六神瓶子 。 怪不得摸起来 很有质感 。 卖这么贵也能好像 一下子就能接受了 。 看到这，一堆网友直接坐不住了。 不是六神你有这技术，真的只做花露水吗？ 距离人民币只 少了两道工序 ？？？ 也算是 合理质疑 了。 我看很刑。 当然，就在一堆网友忙着玩“验钞”梗的时候，也有不少明白人反应过来了。 高人指路见多了， 阎王指路 还是第一次见。 好恶毒的商战。 倒也不是所有话都要听网友的。 对此，六神也是立即表示： 你们不要搞我啊！！！ 有记者联系六神，工作人员说：“标签基材为日化常规印刷材料，未使用印钞纸专用钞票纸。” 这只是36周年的焕新版包装，六神不想变成最后一个版本啊。 不过，这让人好奇，一瓶花露水而已，又不是茅台，防伪有必要这样上纲上线的吗？ 不查不知道，一查吓一跳。现在网上还真的有不少人被真假花露水给整怕了。 有人发出了灵魂拷问： 为什么连花露水都要搞个假的。 如今市面上的六神花露水，大多也就卖十几元到二十元左右。这个价格对消费者来说，往往还没到需要拿着放大镜仔细研究真假的程度。但对造假者来说，却又足够留下利润空间。 并且花露水这个品类，配方相对成熟，原料也比较常见，想调出一个“闻起来差不多”的产品，并没有想象中那么难。久而久之，市面上的假货自然也就多了起来。 而有机构统计，六神花露水在线下零售渠道的销售额份额达到70%以上，可以说是这个品类里当之无愧的头部品牌。也正因为卖得多、认知度高，也让六神成为假货仿制的重点对象。 消费者一旦花正品的钱买到假货，最后被消耗掉的还是对六神的品牌信任。 六神官方显然也注意到了这一点。 这一次， 六神请来了知名设计师潘虎操刀 ，在保留经典视觉基因的基础上，为36周年版本重新设计包装。 可以看到，经典的绿色瓶身、书法Logo和整体版式都保留了下来，潘虎工作室做的，更多还是在原有视觉骨架上增加细节，直接拉高了仿冒门槛。 瓶标上加入椭圆六边形的 “六神原液” 烫金标识，强化产品识别。 瓶身底纹加入 草本植物线条与精细暗纹 ，让原本的标签看起来更丰富、更有层次。 瓶盖也进行了重新设计，瓶盖轮廓加入花朵意象，同时融入海派建筑的拱门造型。 对于，这套设计你怎么看？ 从评论区的反应来看，大部分网友还是认可的。 延续经典 ，像原来的就是好的。 增加了很多细节， 感觉更精致了。 但也有网友吐槽。 跟原来的包装区别不大。 既然是新包装，设计思路不妨 大胆一点 。 细节更多了，辨别真假也更容易了。

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1592.summary: 其在原漫画中的含义并非好喝到哭，而是表达难喝到像尿的极致吐槽。 首发： GrayDesign 近日，瑞幸咖啡与表情包IP暹罗厘普的联名活动因纸袋上的一个表情包引发网友热议，相关话题更是迅速登上了热搜。 28日，瑞幸咖啡与暹罗厘普联名正式开启，以“瑞～到厘普”为主题，推出了系列限定饮品及周边。 然而，很快有网友发现，该联名纸袋上印制的某个表情包， 在原漫画中的真实含义并非“好喝到哭”，而是角色在表达“难喝到像尿”的极致吐槽。 瑞幸这波似乎误将这一个带有负面情绪的表情包，当成了正面宣传素材， 并特别将原表情包的白色纸杯改成了带有瑞幸Logo的杯子，并将其印制在了联名包装上。 相关联名公布之后，随即在社交媒体平台上引发热议。有网友调侃瑞幸选图属于是“不读题就做题”。 也有网友则认为这次“失误”，反而为该联名活动制造了话题度，让更多人“好赖要去买一个看看”。 在我们看来，这起事件也直接体现了在品牌与IP联名中， 大部分品牌往往看中IP的视觉风格和流量价值，却忽略了每个表情在原生内容中的具体含义。 表情包之所以能广泛传播，恰恰因为它精准锚定了某种真实情绪。当这种情绪被反转使用，观众一旦回到原语境，错位感便会立刻显现。 对于瑞幸而言，此次引发的争议或许不会对品牌及相关联名活动造成实质损害， 甚至可能因话题度带动短期销量。 但它却向我们提醒了一个更根本的问题： IP联名不只是借一张好看的图，而是借用一个已经被赋予意义的符号。 符号的意义无法被单方面改写，品牌能做的，要么是尊重它，要么是准备好面对它原本的含义。 对此，不知道你有什么看法？欢迎留言讨论~ 作者公众号：GrayDesign（ID：GrayDesignHK） 更多精彩内容请访问 数英网 - 文章频道 - 项目频道 - 招聘频道

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1592.summary: 不要让大脑长期处于「低分辨率」状态。 来源： 蘇一书 曾经和一个女性朋友在餐厅吃饭。 她点完单，开始向我吐槽一件让她极其恼火的事情。 我的大脑几乎是在听完第一句话的瞬间，就本能地切换到了某种调查程序： 事情起因是什么？ 对方的原话究竟怎么说的？ 在哪个环节信息脱了节，产生的矛盾？ 责任边界在哪里？ 我打断了她，开始追问具体的细节。 我当时的逻辑非常严密： 如果事实的原貌不够完整，所有的情绪宣泄都是虚火，给出的判断也必定廉价。 追问到第三个问题时，她突然停住了，脸色彻底沉了下来： “你这人怎么这么较真？” 我不便再追问，她也断了吐槽的情绪，我们只好切换到其他话题…… 在工作中，类似的事情反复发生：在协作里要求白纸黑字 厘清边界 ，在争论中追问 逻辑前提 ，在沟通中剔除所有修辞 只谈交付 。 结果往往是，对方觉得被冒犯、被审视，我头顶上经常顶着一顶帽子：她很强势。 当年初进职场的我，有时也甚有不忿：为什么职场上基本不用“强势”形容男性呢？ 后来我慢慢想明白了一件事：多数人的社交与协作是建立在模糊之上的—— 含糊的承诺、 模棱两可的推诿、 彼此默认的情绪缓冲。 当一个人说“我很焦虑”、“这事不好办”、“大家都在这么做”时，是习惯于躲在 这些没有形状的词汇 后面。 一个认知清晰的人往往直奔核心：“这件事的目标是什么？”“边界在哪里？”“谁承担责任？” 这种挤掉了所有水分的直截了当，会瞬间撕下对方用于保护自尊的伪装，让人感到被审视与逼仄。 1、“强势”和“清晰”的差异 但“强势”和“清晰”其实是两套底层系统。我需要为自己“正名”下： 如果把两者的内核拆开，你会发现它们在每一个维度上都完全相反： 1）驱动力完全不同 专断型强势，核心在 人 。 它本质是对权力的索取，为了维持自我权威和那点不可动摇的正确感，必须压制对方、掌控全场——它的终点是“我要赢”。 而真正的清晰，核心在 事 。 它的驱动力从来不是支配他人，而是为了看清事实原貌，降低系统的混乱与认知负荷。 2）面对异议与反驳时，反应不同 强势的人把异议当成挑衅，会本能地调动情绪去捍卫结论，绝不允许权威受损； 清晰的人把新证据当成修正的契机，一旦逻辑或事实被推翻，他们随时可以极其平静地承认：“我之前的判断错了。” 3）使用的话语结构不同 强势者的语言充斥着居高临下的价值评判和命令句——“你必须怎样”、“这根本不对”； 清晰者的语言则专注于前提、条件与推论——“如果前提是A，那么B才成立”、“在什么边界条件下，这个结论有效”。不搞道德审判，只做逻辑推导。 4）对“边界”的认知完全相反 强势往往伴随着边界侵略，试图粗暴地改造他人的想法，把自己的意志强加于人； 清晰则是在严防自己的边界。清晰的人清楚知道哪些事属于外部变量、不可控制，因此能冷酷地撤回注意力，绝不在他人的人生里指手画脚。 看出两者的差别了吗？ 真正的清晰，是对客

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1593.summary: 彻底坐实了奢品公关的草台班子。 原标题：Tiffany这场“公关灾难”，彻底坐实了奢品公关的草台 一盒月饼，竟然让Tiffany疯狂掉粉，滤镜全碎…… 相信你刷到了（如果你知道过程，也可以跳过直接看点评。这篇内容其实是我被多个读者催更催的，感谢你们的鞭策）。 成都一位姑娘，曾在Tiffany专柜十几分钟刷了二十多万。就这么一位掏钱眼睛都不眨的vip客户，中秋前没等来品牌承诺送的Tiffany月饼礼盒，主动一问，销售说：寄错人了，给了别的客人，下次有礼物再想着您。 消费者觉得奢侈品的体验很差，发小红书吐槽。 后面的剧情就开始往荒诞剧一路狂奔： 销售疯狂骚扰顾客，希望删帖。 门店副经理一通小作文的开场白，竟然还报自己的"艺名"…… 补偿方案更扯， 称二十块钱的散装桃酥，而Tiffany月饼礼盒据说在二手平台被卖到了2000块。 20块，2000块，20万，三个数字，恰好形成了巨大的反差！ 姑娘不删帖，结果，小红书不仅帖子被投诉消失，账号直接"安全限制"，差点封号了。 9月28日，"Tiffany月饼""Tiffany捂嘴""Tiffany中国区负责人致歉"齐刷刷挂上热搜！ 只有那家被迫"联名"的宫廷糕点铺，喜提泼天流量。 当晚，品牌方才做出实质性反应。 该消费者发文表示，Tiffany中国区零售负责人已向其发送邮件致歉。 在曝光的邮件截图中，该负责人称“高度重视您反映的问题，并已将其列为优先处理事项”，并“代表零售团队郑重致歉”。 对于这份迟来的官方道歉，当事人要求，品牌方需要就礼盒为何被擅自转送、桃酥补偿方案的决策过程、以及个人账号被限制的原因给出全面、可核验的书面解释。 最新的消息是：Tiffany中国零售管理团队已向该消费者披露了内部调查结果，承认系门店运营人员“地址拷贝错误”所致，并提出了对涉事员工进行处理、设立客诉升级机制、删除客户隐私地址等整改措施。品牌方甚至提出由负责人亲自飞往消费者所在地当面致歉。 但消费者依然不买账坚持。 大叔捋完整个时间线，只有一个感受： 这哪是百年奢侈品牌，这分明就是草台班子。 整个危机应对全程，几乎全错，堪称“公关灾难”。 大叔总结成3个关键错误，希望所有奢侈品品牌别再犯了。 1、捂嘴（小红书删帖），就 是给危机在“加热”。 先说最蠢的一步，但几乎所有公关都在干这个事。 危机公关有句老话，大叔说过很多遍： 问题本身往往不是最致命的，应对问题的方式才是。 月饼寄错，说破天是个服务失误，道个歉、马上补一份、捋一遍内部流程，翻不起大浪。消费者要的是什么？是个态度，是你把她当回事。 Tiffany怎么做的？先不主动告知，等客户自己来问； 问了，轻飘飘一句"下次补"； 客户在小红书吐个槽，不想着解决问题，先想着解决发帖子的人。 据姑娘说，门店一遍遍打电话、发消息劝她删笔记。被拒之后，她的小红书账号就开始提示"安全限制、访问频繁"，笔

https://www.digitaling.com/articles/1593.summary: 潮玩市场的胜负手，已从“赌爆款”转向系统化养成IP的能力。 作者：梁多多，来源： 20社 中秋节，一个5厘米高的搪胶娃娃站在高高垒起来的椅子上，对着窗外的夜色举起一块方便面饼，博主@Biety呆呆 在标题里写道， “别不开心了，YOYO请你看月亮”。 帖子很快被数万人点赞和转发。评论区，陆续有人晒出YOYO举鱼灯、月饼、螃蟹等的图片。 这个由名创优品推出的原创IP，上市至今不过15个月。 从2025年6月的一张陌生面孔，到今年8月单月全球销售额突破2亿元，YOYO刷新了中国原创IP的成长速度。 一个原创IP从诞生到实现亿级商业化，常规路径需要3到5年的内容沉淀与社群积累。没有影视和动画加持的YOYO，凭极简视觉符号、用户自发二创与庞大的渠道网络，把IP成长周期压缩了近三分之二。 更关键的是， 这还是名创优品的首个原创艺术家IP。 也就是说，这家在大众认知中以渠道和IP联名见长的公司，正在快速积累起自有内容资产。国元国际分析师李承儒在研报中指出，名创优品正在从过去的“IP整合－供应链转化－渠道变现”的线性模式，升级为构建一个能够自我循环、自我生长的自有IP生态。 当一个消费品牌开始自己孵化IP，“渠道优势”能否替代“内容底座”？ 名创优品验证的究竟是“原创IP的运营能力”，还是“一次高效率爆款的打造能力”？ 01 一个IP是怎么“长”出来的：YOYO养成记 YOYO最值得观察的，不只是销售数字本身，而是它在短时间内完成了从“一个新角色”到“具有商业规模的IP”的过程。 这个IP的创作原点，是 艺术家王涌泉对孩童观察世界状态的具象化 。整个造型十分简单，因为越简单大家越容易记住，也越容易把自己的情绪投射进去。这刚好承接了当代年轻人的轻治愈需求。 YOYO尺寸小巧，方便出现在日常生活场景中。名创优品集团副总裁兼首席营销官刘晓彬透露，YOYO初期定价29.9元和ICONBOX轻量化盲盒形态，也是为了降低用户的决策门槛。 墨墨是资深潮玩玩家，也是一名潮玩从业者。她表示，过去大家买潮玩是因为喜欢某个IP，买回来摆在家里做收藏。现在潮玩可以当包挂，也可以摆到办公桌上，成了一种身份认同，也是“精神世界的一种外化”。 墨墨是在网上刷到“YOYO举万物”帖子入坑的。在这些帖子里，YOYO举着数据线、水果、叶子等一切大家能想象到的东西。尤其是她小小的身体经常举着比自己大不少的东西，瞬间戳中了打工人的共鸣和自嘲，制造出一系列热梗。 今年1-8月，YOYO累计话题浏览量达到19亿。 实际上， YOYO被粉丝们津津乐道的“手举”功能，一开始只是开放的表达形态，却在客观上为后续二创和互动埋下了物理基础。 IP在这个时候不再是品牌灌输的符号，而是用户共同 “养成” 的陪伴。 名创优品把这件事总结为一句话： 好IP是半成品。 创作者给出基础形象和世界观，消费者基于自己的生活情绪和社交表达，继

https://www.digitaling.com/projects/3785.summary: 从清晨的社区，到午后的古城，再到夜晚的朝天门——2026年久久公益节，我们 把一条Citywalk路线，变成了一整天的善意动线。 这一天，很多互不相识的人，各自做了一件小事： 9月9日清晨，社区里的一位女孩顺手帮邻居收了快递； 上午，商场的等位区，等咖啡的年轻人扫了码、捐了步； 下午，南头古城的街巷里，女孩集到了第三朵小红花印章； 傍晚，红山动物园，一个孩子举着贴纸问：“小红花是什么意思？” 夜晚，5000架无人机从江面升起，两江四岸之间拼出一朵巨大的小红花。 ——整座城市，抬起了头。 视频 这些互不相识的人，在同一天里，各自完成了一件小事。 我们管这一天，叫 「好事发生的一天」。 公益最大的敌人，不是冷漠，是"距离感" 项目启动前，我们反复讨论一个问题： 为什么越来越多年轻人说自己"想做公益"，最后却没有行动？ 数据给了我们一个反直觉的答案：放弃的节点，大多不在"不想做"，而在"特地做"。公益被默认成一件需要专门登录、专门搜索、专门奔赴的事。而当代人的生活节奏，恰恰很难"特地"做一件事。 所以我们要解决的问题是—— 如何让做好事，变得像"路过买杯咖啡"一样自然？ 好事不该等人专程奔赴，它应该出现在人们本来就要走的路上。 于是我们把核心创意，定为 —— 「好事发生的一天」，一条顺路做好事的 Citywalk 路线。 善意不设专场，只在这条路上，等你顺路。 清晨·小社区：好事就在邻里之间。 路线的第一站，是每个人下楼就能到的地方。 帮邻居取快递、停下来欣赏一幅画、读一首诗——这些日常小事，都被记录为"好事"。今年，「好事社区」已经记录下了 46 万+件身边好事。 一条留言很打动我们："这些事听起来很小，小到一幅画、一首诗、一个对着哈哈镜的微笑。社区不大，但能做的是不少。" 上午·商场：等人的一分钟，也能做好事。 商场里似乎总有人在等待——等朋友、等咖啡、等扶梯、等电影开场。 我们在全国的商场都设置了小红花街区装置。 你不用专程找它，它就在必经的动线上。等人的一分钟，捐个步、玩个游戏、许个心愿、揭下一张好事签、欣赏一幅星星孩子的画——善意就这么顺路发生了。 商场，从消费空间变成了公益的触点。 小红花摊位前，有人取走了今天的"好食"——一份原本可能被浪费的余量食物，变成了一次"刚刚好"的日常善行，它可以很轻，轻到从"好好吃饭、不浪费"这件小事开始。 下午 · 南头古城：Citywalk时，顺路做件好事。 南头古城是深圳年轻人最喜欢闲逛的地方之一。我们没有把它变成一场传统的公益展，而是顺着古城的街巷动线，设计了一套灵巧有趣的装置，让它成为一条“一块做好事”的路。 街角有孩子们的公益画展，转角有小红花气模装置，咖啡馆门口可以扫码捐步，集章点顺便提醒你"今天也可以做一件好事"。 看展、逛街、集章、发朋友圈，一气呵成 ——公益不是专程任务，而是 Citywalk 路线上的

https://www.digitaling.com/projects/3788.summary: 视频 创新往往来自一个小细节的改变。 当人们拿起冰镇酒杯时，桌上就会多出一个水印。 一般人只是擦掉，喜力注意到这点，把它变成了品牌标志，希望人们看到时会想要把它带回家。 品牌联合荷兰设计工作室 NPK Design重新设计了一款星标玻璃杯。杯底饰以品牌最具辨识度的五角星标志，并贯穿整个杯身，杯底边缘会凝结水汽。当有人拿起杯子时，杯底会留下五角星水印。 看似简单的形状，制作起来却很困难。 据npk称，玻璃制造商最初认为这种形状无法大规模生产。设计师运用其模具工程方面的经验，制作出高度逼真的有机玻璃模型，并对其抓握力、稳定性、倾倒和饮用舒适度进行了测试，确定了最终形态。 喜力表示，这款酒杯的研发目的不仅仅是为了提升外观。它的高度和形状还能更好地展现酒香、呈现酒体并保持泡沫持久，而符合人体工学的杯身设计则为顾客和酒吧工作人员提供了舒适的握持感。 相关推荐阅读： Lululemon：汉密尔顿的跨界休息日 lululemon×汪顺：听说，你也有个“烦人”的队友 lululemon新春主题短片：春天，重复如新 On昂跑Asia Fit：在无感之后，感受全新的当下 喜力啤酒：与其发冗长语音，不如出来喝一杯吧！ 喜力找机器人开啤酒，交给它就闹心吧 健力士：毫无违和感的换字游戏 哈根达斯×时代啤酒：两块广告牌，当街聊起了暧昧 加拿大啤酒广告：一夜之间，麦田上长出了啤酒罐 更多精彩内容请访问 数英网 - 文章频道 - 项目频道 - 招聘频道

https://www.digitaling.com/projects/3788.summary: 最近，播 broadcast 官宣演员卢昱晓成为品牌大使，并与 NOWNESS 共同带来 2026 冬季品牌大片《挥动季候风·故乡》。 从春夏的 《风辞典》 到秋冬的《挥动季候风》，这一年，播好像一直在追着“风”走的——春天的风，藏着南方潮湿的空气、旧屋窗缝和个人记忆；到了冬天，风从故乡吹来，也引出了另一个问题： 当人离开故乡，那些曾经裹挟着她的风，吹向了哪里？ 《挥动季候风·故乡》 文案 房间把风缩得很小。 那时候我还不知道， 画画并不真的从白纸开始。 我从小熟悉的光线和冷暖， 还有人与人相处的距离， 早在落笔以前， 就成了我看世界的方式。 风大时，纸页被轻轻掀起， 线条偶尔偏离。 我不急着纠正。 有些偏离， 本来就是画的一部分。 慢慢发现， 一阵风也不是空的。 它从一个地方吹来， 带着那里的温度和气味。 一路向前， 也沾上新的天气。 世界在变， 风也不会停。 我继续走， 继续看。 风来的时候， 就借它起势。 风起时， 我也起身。 影片中，卢昱晓以一个创作者的身份出现。 她拿起画笔，经过街道、老房与郊野；停下来观察光线、植物和周围细小的变化，也慢慢意识到：一幅画并不真正从白纸开始。 和春季的《风辞典》不同，在这支片子里，风被用来隐喻，一个人最早在故乡的经历。 来自故乡的风，或暴烈或温柔，它们影响着我们第一次认识天气的冷暖、光落下来的方向，也建立起我们最早的审美、习惯和观看世界的方法。 后来，随着人走向更远的地方，这些经验也跟着人一起远行。 但就像镜头中的卢昱晓一直身处身流动世界中，风也不是一成不变的。 借由卢昱晓“对世界保持感受力”的个性，播也强调人在变化的环境里依然保有自己的判断力和节奏。 就像季候风。它从一个地方吹向另一个地方，带着来处的温度、水汽和气味，又在途中形成新的天气。 人也是如此。这些来处会影响一个人，但我们依然可以按照自己的速度，一边被新的城市、新的经历改变，一边带着自己最初形成的那部分感受，继续往前。 相关推荐阅读： 播×倪妮：在潮湿的南方，翻翻风 裘真×宋佳：不谈主义，好好经历 edition×文淇：拥抱好心情 裘真×春夏《时间容器》：世界是我的倒影 更多精彩内容请访问 数英网 - 文章频道 - 项目频道 - 招聘频道

https://www.digitaling.com/projects/3789.summary: 《Money Relationships》 《与钱相处》 钱是很多人生活里绕不开的压力，却也是一个不少人不太愿意谈的话题。 这一次，南非四大银行之一Nedbank没有从“如何存钱”“如何避免负债”这些熟悉的金融话题切入，而是把目光放到了人与钱本身的关系上。在这支名为《Money Relationships》的短片里，钱甚至有了自己的名字：Ben。 故事一开始，Sam正处在人生的上升期。刚刚升职的他，在庆祝派对上遇到了Ben。 Ben看起来是个很有魅力的人。他自信、慷慨，似乎总知道哪里有更好的生活，也总能帮Sam打开一扇通往新世界的门。 对刚刚升职、收入增加的Sam来说，这样的朋友很难拒绝。于是， Sam开始跟着Ben进入原本不属于自己的生活。 更好的衣服、更高级的场所、更昂贵的消费……随着收入增加，Sam似乎也终于拥有了“过上更好生活”的资格。 而Ben就在旁边，不断鼓励着他。 一开始，这一切看起来甚至有些令人羡慕。谁会拒绝更好的生活呢？ 但问题也正是在这里开始发生。 当消费越来越高，仅靠收入已经无法支撑这样的生活时，Sam开始做出一些不同寻常的财务决定。 先是借钱。再后来，是越来越危险的赌博。 Ben却始终陪在身边。 他没有阻止Sam，反而像一个永远站在旁边怂恿你的朋友，让Sam觉得自己只是暂时超支，或者只要下一次赢回来，一切就能重新回到正轨。 但 钱越借越多，风险也越来越大。 曾经因为升职而意气风发的Sam，开始一点点失去原本拥有的东西。事业、生活、关系，甚至是对自己的控制。 故事最后，Sam已经彻底陷入财务危机。 曾经光鲜亮丽的生活消失了，只剩下一个破败的旅馆房间。而此时，Ben终于揭开了自己的真实身份。他根本不是Sam认识的新朋友。 他就是Money。 回头再看，前面发生的一切突然都有了新的解释。 Ben为什么总能带Sam进入更好的地方？ 因为 钱可以替你打开很多扇门。 Ben为什么总在鼓励Sam享受更好的生活？ 因为 钱本身就很容易让人产生欲望。 Nedbank这次没有把“理财”拍成一堂枯燥的金融课，而是借一个男人的坠落，把那些平时不太愿意面对的财务问题，变成了一场看得见的“关系”。真正需要被重新审视的，可能从来不只是账户里的数字，而是我们究竟把钱当成了什么，又让它在自己的生活里占据了什么位置。 相关推荐阅读： 莱利银行微电影：你的银行账户里有秘密吗？ 瞬间财富自由？这支广告打工人看完想跑路 泰国金融广告：天降横祸，房子被巨人口水砸了 更多精彩内容请访问 数英网 - 文章频道 - 项目频道 - 招聘频道
